name: Israel & the Israel of God
about: Who Israel is, the church, and Zionism.

teachings.title: The inheritance belongs to all in Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The land promise is fulfilled in the resurrection and the inheritance passes to all who have put on Christ, so Christians who give it away to modern Zionism for politics are like Esau selling his birthright.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 8:7–10**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people*

The promise to occupy the land will be fulfilled for the Old Testament believers, in the resurrection. The only "Zionism" that matters is Christ Jesus on His throne. The inheritance is passed to all who have put on Christ.

**Romans 8:14–17**
*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together*.

This promise, the inheritance and blessings, is the heritage of all believers, from Adam and Abel, Seth and Noah, through every professing Christian today.

The spirit of Esau, who forsook his inheritance for a bowl of pottage, lives in Christians, who for political expediency seek to give it away.

**Hebrews 12:14–17**
*Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled; Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.*

This tearful repentance will be the case for many in the end times. Those who placed modern politics and bad theology above the joy unspeakable found in Jesus for all who believe, Jew or Gentile. Man or woman. Bond or free.

teachings.title: Zion, the redeemed bride of Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Zion and Jerusalem are a picture of the believer, the redeemed bride of Christ whom He jealously protects and will perfect as the New Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
But, Zion, like believers, stained crimson in sin, has a redeemer. And, like His church, Jerusalem is His bride, made perfect and decked in the finest array, fit for the King.

**Isaiah 61:10**
*I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.*

**Isaiah 62:1–7**
*For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth. And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name. Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God. Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married. For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee. I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.*

Zion, and Jerusalem, are a picture of the believer. A bride of Christ, made precious by His redemption, protecting it like a jealous husband;

**Zechariah 1:14**
*So the angel that communed with me said unto me, Cry thou, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.*

**Isaiah 54:5–7**
*For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called. For the LORD hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God. For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.*

In the end, we shall see New Jerusalem, upon his holy hill, Zion. Perfected as a picture of his people, His bride;

**Revelation 21:1–2**
*And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea. And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.*

This is the promise of his holy place, how much more so is it the promise for those who have trusted in Christ. In an unmovable Rock, the cornerstone laid in Zion. The Rock of our salvation, we who are the bride of Christ. Amen

teachings.title: Mount Zion, chosen of God
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Zion is holy because God placed His name there and separated it for His purposes, the place of Christ's sacrifice and future reign, not because its people are holy.
teachings.text:
Mount Zion, Jerusalem, is often referenced and praised as the place God chose to place His name. His holy city, the mountain providing natural protection on 3 sides, situated perfectly. A river running through the fertile valley. The setting where Abraham brought Issac. Where God prepared Himself a sacrifice. Where Jesus was slain and rose again, and where He will reign in the Kingdom to come.

The name, Zion, means a “monument; raised up; sepulcher,” the place of the tomb, hewn out of rock, the site of Christ's burial. Chosen by God.

Jerusalem, the city isn't a lonely peak, but rather a settlement nestled within a protective bowl of higher terrain, with Mt Moriah and the mount of Olives part of the limestone rings, defending the area.

**Psalm 125:1–2**
*They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever. As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever.*

Beautiful for situation, a perfect location, the city if the great King on its north face.

**Psalm 132:13–14**
*For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.*

**1 Peter 2:5–6**
*Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.*

The shelter of Zion, the cornerstone of which is Christ, is where Jesus returns to in the end times, with the 144,000 witnesses.

**Revelation 14:1**
*And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.*

The defenses of this holy mountain were enough to dissuade kings and armies.

Sennacherib, of Assyria, the most powerful emperor of the ancient world, invaded Judah with a massive army of 185,000 soldiers.

He sent his top military commanders to the walls of Jerusalem, fiercely mocking King Hezekiah and blaspheming God, confidently expecting the city to fall just like every other nation before it.

Hezekiah called out to the Lord for protection of the city.

**2 Kings 19:16–19**
*LORD, bow down thine ear, and hear: open, LORD, thine eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherib, which hath sent him to reproach the living God. Of a truth, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands, And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them. Now therefore, O LORD our God, I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD God, even thou only.*

And God harkened to the prayer, for His own purposes and will;

**2 Kings 19:32–34**
*Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

Zion is defended for His own sake, because He placed His name there, and for the promise made to David that out of Zion shall come a King.

**Romans 11:26–27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Zion is holy, because it has been separated unto the purposes of God.

It is not holy because the people there are holy. God allowed Babylon to raze the city and remove the people. Jesus decreed that Jerusalem would fall, and in 70AD it did. With the end times approaching, the city is considered wicked;

teachings.title: Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The blessing on the nation whose God is the Lord is open to any people who trust Him, for those in Christ are Abraham's seed, and Israel was chosen to be a light to the Gentiles.
teachings.text:
Like all good spiritual songs, **Psalm 33** is dripping with doctrine, especially the inspired Psalms, because:

*For the word of the LORD is right; and all his works are done in truth*

His word and works are right and truth. Foundational doctrine. Amen.

*He loveth righteousness and judgment: the earth is full of the goodness of the LORD.* Again, I say, Amen!

*By the word of the LORD were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth*.

A song about singing the praises of the Lord that also teaches why. The creation of all things, by His Word, and brought into being by inspiration. The hosts of Heaven, the gatherings of the sea. His truth and righteous judgment.

*Let all the earth fear the LORD: let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him.* Amen, amen, amen!

We should sing of His glory. Why? Because of His might, we should fear Him, Who spoke all things into being. Who commanded and it was done. Whose Word made the foundations stand fast. Amen!

When taken as an instrument of teaching, Psalms serve to give perfect understanding to those that are singing. Models of prayer and adoration, given as examples and encouragement to those that fear the Lord.

*The LORD bringeth the counsel of the heathen to nought: he maketh the devices of the people of none effect.*

The pride and arrogance of man, who without God, or His wisdom, attempt to plan their greatness, only to be dashed against the Rock. Only to have it all come to nothing.

Contrast this futility with this truth; *The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations*.

The knowledge of His ways, revealed by His word, through the oracles and prophets of God, bless a people.

*Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD; and the people whom he hath chosen for his own inheritance.*

Note this is inclusive, not exclusive to one nation. Those He hath chosen for His own inheritance, any people that trust in Him, any nation that makes Him their God, is blessed.

**Galatians 3:29**
*And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

Because believers are elect in Christ, to receive these blessings as joint-heirs.

**Romans 8:16–17**
*The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.*

This offer is extended to the whole world. At the time of David, the king understood that Israel was elected to be a beacon of God's light, not an elitist and special nation, to only know the true God.

As the Bible says in **Isaiah 49:6** *I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.*

The only advantage Israel had was receiving the oracles of God, and the promise to David to bring about the Christ from his line, and stewardship of the city where He chose to place His name. Otherwise they'd have been as Sodom.

teachings.title: Salvation is the wall
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Jerusalem's wall of fire shows God's salvation as His people's defense, and the kingdom is now for believers of all nations while unbelievers are cast out.
teachings.text:
Here in **Zechariah 2**, we see the prophet again encouraging the people to rebuild and restore, knowing that the Lord is with them and will be their strength, if they only keep His ways.

The angel that Zechariah sees in his vision, like those that appeared to Ezekiel and John, is measuring, this time the size of the city, Jerusalem. The angels speak, and the one saying to tell Zechariah that the city will be so large, with the multitude of men and cattle, that there isn't a physical wall to protect them, but a wall of fire, the glory of God in her midst.

Similarly, we see in Isaiah this same concept, that God's Salvation is the wall. His salvation is the bulwark.

The second major theme repeated from Isaiah is the understanding that all nations shall flow into the city, to Zion. The nation of the righteous who keeps the truth.

This has been consistently the promise of God for Judah. And in the Old Testament times of Zerubbabel, and Ezra and Nehemiah, it was a promise to the physical nation, as well as a prophecy of the end times Kingdom that would include all people who believed. That He shall choose Jerusalem again.

And when Jesus came, the Messiah, they slew Him and hanged Him on a tree. So it becomes what could have been.

So now, in the New and better Testament, there is a similar, but different Kingdom. A millennial Kingdom of believers from all nations, still. And the peace of swords becoming plowshares. But the children of the Kingdom shall be cast out for unbelief.

Salvation is the wall. Without faith and trust in that, there is no part for them. But all those that believe are given the inheritance and blessings, the promises of God.

teachings.title: The inheritance was never exclusive to the Jews
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Even Ezekiel gives believing strangers the same inheritance as the tribes, showing God's promises were always for all who believe on Christ, never a genetic favor to Jews.
teachings.text:
Finally, in the final verse of Ezekiel 47, we are again shown that this The empire and Kingdom would not be exclusive to the Hebrews. The 12 tribes of Israel given land, Joseph's double portion making up for the Levites, are joined by strangers among them, the circumcised of the heart talked about in chapter 46.

These Gentiles are given the same inheritance, the same birthright of those among the tribes of Israel. Wherever they sojourn, in whatever tribe they settle, there it will be for them and inheritance.

**Ephesians 2:12-19**
*That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world: But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby: And came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh. For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father. Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God*

This shows regardless of the covenant, regardless of which Testament that man was under, it was never exclusive to the Jews. Never. It was always about those circumcised of the heart and believing on Christ, calling upon His name.

There is neither Jew nor Greek.

The Dispensationalist Zionists seek to exclude the Gentiles from the inheritance and the promises. To say that Jews are the seed of Abraham, rather than all who believe on THE seed, being singular; Christ Jesus.

They ignore the inconvenient truths in the New Testament, but you can see that they also ignore those prophecies in the Old.

They have the spirit of Edom, like Esau, giving away the inheritance for pottage.

God's redemptive plan was ALWAYS to include people from every nation, kindred and tongue. It always did, as we see in multiple OT figures who came to believe. Many grafted into the line of Christ (Tamar, Ruth, Rahab, likely also Bathsheba).

The genetic false gospel of special favors to the Jews was always unbiblical. Regardless of how the prophecies ultimately played out.

teachings.title: Circumcision of the heart is what matters
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Scripture moves from circumcision of the flesh to pleas for circumcised hearts until in the New Testament only circumcision of the heart counts, open to believing Gentiles.
teachings.text:
Looking back at **Ezekiel 44**, we find the giving of ordinances for the priests and the temple, beginning with the command that the East Gate, which the presence of the Lord would enter through, would remain shut and not be for any man to enter, but for the prince, or king, to enter via a porch entrance of the gate, a smaller door within it. That he would enter and sit before it to eat bread before the Lord, and go out the same.

Ezekiel is then taken to the North Gate, and falls to his knees when he sees the glory of the Lord filling the house of the Lord, the temple.

He is again instructed to see with his eyes and hear with his ears, that he may tell others. This command is repeatedly used in Ezekiel, and is found throughout scripture in other contexts as instructions for the righteous. For the saved. We are told to observe, hear and repeat to others.

Even to the rebellious. We are to preach His word and ways to the lost, and if they don't heed, like the man who ignores the warning trumpet, it is on them.

Here, God says to Israel, let this teaching *suffice you of all your abominations.* He is telling them what they need to do to get right.

God talks about the bringing in of strangers, foreigners (and their idols), who are not His people, into the house of the Lord, polluting it. Note, that He sets aside the allowance of non-Israelites who are either circumcised of the heart, or flesh. Who are saved believers or are assimilated into the nation.

The provision for the circumcision of the heart among strangers seems to be a broadening of the terms. In other places, there has been an appeal for the children of Israel to circumcise their hearts towards the Lord. Such as the appeal to the rebellious people in **Deuteronomy 10:6** *Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.* An appeal repeated several times, including

**Jeremiah 4:4**
*Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: lest my fury come forth like fire, and burn that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.*

In the New Testament, it is only the circumcision of the heart that is welcome to the Lord.

**Romans 2:28-29**
*For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God*.

So, we see the progression. Hebrews after the flesh are circumcised, beginning with Abraham. In the wilderness, mostly in Deuteronomy and Leviticus, the circumcised of the flesh are asked to circumcise their hearts as well.

By the beginning of captivity, it is a plea to get saved, and avoid the coming destruction.

Here, in the midst of the captivity, when discussing an OT Temple that could be, it is included to count for Gentiles who believed.

In the New Testament, it becomes the only circumcision that matters.

teachings.title: Restored not for their sakes but His name's
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God restored Israel from captivity not because they deserved it but for His holy name's sake, and sometimes He blesses us the same way to sanctify His name.
teachings.text:
Having prophesied against Israel, throughout Judah and earning of their coming judgment, and having prophesied against the heathen nations that surround them for laughing at their calamity, saying "Aha!" and seeking to take advantage of the situation, God's word upon Ezekiel begins to shift towards prophecy of restoration and redemption in the future.

Preaching to the mountains, to the desolate land filled with wastes, the Lord says He will fill up the land, increase the people, the corn, the beasts, and make the desolate overflow. To bring back to life that which was dead. That all will know, He is the Lord.

Dual meaning here, that is the promise of restoring Jerusalem after the Babylonian captivity, and as we will see, a future restoration of His people Israel, under a new covenant and promise.

First we should note, it is not because of the Jews that God would restore them from captivity;

*But I had pity for mine holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the heathen, whither they went. Therefore say unto the house of Israel, thus saith the Lord God; I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went.*

Just as we have seen elsewhere, it is always His holy name and the city where He chose to place it. Not the people.

God is doing this despite their ways, because they caused His holy name to be blasphemed among the heathen.

Sometimes we are blessed openly, not because we deserve it, but because our sins have given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme Him.

Sometimes we are blessed simply to sanctify His name.

teachings.title: Surnamed by the name of Israel
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Christians become the elect of Israel by adoption, called by His name and given a new name like Jacob.
teachings.text:
*For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.*

This verse, a direct reference to Cyrus, is also a prophecy of Christians, under Jesus. Made sons of God and co-heirs with Christ. Those called by His name. The elect of Israel. That we are given God as a surname, adopted as sons and daughters in Him.

For Jacob was His servant to bring about the Messiah, and the elect of Israel, the name Jacob is given by the Lord after a night of wrestling with Him over his past, and facing his future.

Knowing Esau was riding towards him, with 400 men, Jacob went by himself to pray. And after lasting the night, prevailing, and being made lame by a touch of God to his hip, he relented to God's will, and was renamed Israel in **Genesis 32:28**.

We become the elect of Israel by adoption. And we are called by His name, in Christ.

And like Jacob, given a new name in the resurrection.

**Revelation 2:17**
*He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.*

Amen

teachings.title: Elect according to grace, not heritage
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Isaiah 44:5 foretells Christians called the Lord's, Jews claiming Jacob, and others claiming Israel, while God's elect are elect by grace.
teachings.text:
Again, a wonderful picture of salvation and redemption by the Lord God, upon His servants who are Israel. The same believers in the Old Testament and New. The living waters promised in Christ.

*One shall say, I am the Lord's; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel*.

I believe this is a clear prophecy of what has become the situation after Jesus ascension, and here in these last days.

Christians say we are the Lord's, and Jews of the 1st century, "We are of Jacob." And now, those who claim to be Israel.

It also reflects the reality of Isaiah's time. The saved believers, the southern kingdom of Judah and the northern kingdom of Israel.

Elect according to grace. Those who believe they are elect according to heritage. Those who claim election while being far from Him.

That's what my thoughts are in this, and God reminds us, He is in charge over all.

*Thus saith the Lord the King of Israel, and his redeemer the Lord of hosts; I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God. And who, as I, shall call, and shall declare it, and set it in order for me, since I appointed the ancient people? and the things that are coming, and shall come, let them shew unto them.*

There is no God besides Him. Fear not. We who trust in Him shall not be ashamed.

teachings.title: The tabernacle of David raised up
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Unbelieving Israel was disowned like the heathen, while the fallen tabernacle of David is raised in Christ for the remnant of Gentiles called by His name.
teachings.text:
The word of the Lord, as preached by Amos, contains very clear language and promises. Not as rich in dark saying and vague symbols as people portray the books of the prophets.

He tells Amos, smite the lintel of the door that the posts shake and fall on the heads of the Israelites, and the Lord will slay all of them with the sword. A reverse Passover, where the blood of the lamb on the lintel saved the people.

No matter where they seek to hide, the Lord shall have their lives. Dug underground to Hell, the tops of mountains, the bottom of the sea, even surrendering to captivity, there is no escaping the wrath against Israel, nor the end times wrath it pictures.

The Lord is mighty, and all powerful. Amen! The Lord is His name.

*Are ye not as children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel? saith the Lord. Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?*

The Israelites of the Northern Kingdom are utterly disowned. No better than the Ethiopian. Just as He took the children of Israel from Egypt, He says, so too He took the Philistines from Caphtor, which is Crete and the Syrians from Southern Babylon, which is Kir. They aren't the only nation taken and moved by God to a new land, and made mighty. And they aren't the only people He chooses to destroy.

It is humbling to know He thinks no more of these people, called by His name and who betrayed Him, than the heathen nations who are their enemies.

*Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.*

Because that remnant of Jacob will lead to Christ, and the promise the Lord made unto David, and the place, Jerusalem, which He placed His name, in Jesus.

He sifted them as He does all nations. And all the sinners of His people slain. Wew.

With the promise of wrath and destruction, God the long-suffering and merciful offers that blessed hope.

*In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.*

Jesus, the Son of David, restored to His throne in His Kingdom. And the promise is not just to believing Israel, or to the "Jews," but even to Edom, to the heathen which are called by His name. To the remnant of the Gentiles that believe on Christ. His people, Israel, to the paradise of His eternal Kingdom.

A*nd they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God*.

teachings.title: A remnant according to the election of grace
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God saves or condemns by belief and unbelief, not ethnicity or nation: Israel's branches were broken off for unbelief, Gentiles are grafted in by faith, and God's children are Abraham's seed by faith.
teachings.text:
**2 Peter 3:9**
*The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.*

**Romans 11:1-5**
*I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life. But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.*

It is important to recognize that it isn't by ethnicity or nation that God saves or condemns, but by belief and unbelieving.

The destruction of the Northern Kingdom of Israel was for their unbelief. The eventual destruction of Judea was for rejecting Christ. At the end of the world, on that great and terrible day of the Lord, the wrath will come on the whole earth for unbelief, the righteous remnant spared, and Jesus will get rule with all His saints.

**Romans 11:15-21,30-32**
*For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead? For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.*.. *For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.*

The love of God is conditional on belief in His word. The Bible says, without faith it is impossible to please God. His children are children by faith, adopted as sons of God through Christ. Heirs according to His promise, made Abraham's seed for belief.

Those that remain in unbelief are cast into the fire by their own choice. By their own counsels.

teachings.title: Wild grapes, the wild olive and the true vine
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God found the patriarchs as wild grapes, as the Gentiles are a wild olive grafted in, and Christ is the root and true vine from which unbelieving Ephraim is cut off.
teachings.text:
The curse of Ephraim by the Lord, as spoken by the prophet Hosea in the Spirit. Their threshing floors are empty, their winepress fails them, they are scattered to Egypt and Assyria. They no longer can offer sacrifice to the Lord, but rather eat of polluted bread.

Their judgment has come. They were warned. All Israel shall see the judgment. The prophets driven mad by their inequities, hated in the house of God by the people.

*They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah*, the rape of the Levite's concubine by the sodomites in Benjamin, back in **Judges 19**. The abominations that nearly destroyed Benjamin utterly.

The Lord laments that in Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, He found a people as wild grapes in the wilderness. That they were as the first ripe figs of the early summer.

This reminds us of the comparison to wild vine of the gentiles, grafted in;

**Romans 11:11-21**
*For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.*

The root is Christ. He is the true vine. But if Gentiles were graft in by the gospel, so too were the original branches of the patriarchs. Wild grapes the Lord prepared a vineyard for. Here, He is about to hew off a branch in Ephraim, and cast it into the fire.

teachings.title: Loammi: ye are not my people
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Hosea's children declare God's mercy removed from Israel and that they are not His people, refuting dispensationalism, while the promise of sons of the living God is fulfilled in Christ.
teachings.text:
Poor Hosea, the prophet with the burden of the Lord to make his very life a living parable against Israel. To marry a whore, representing the whoredoms of Israel, chasing after false gods.

To have a son, named after the place, Jezreel, where Jehu slew the house of Ahab. Where blood would be avenged by the Lord to end the kingdom of Israel.

Then to have a daughter, Loruhamah, meaning that God's mercy was no longer upon the northern kingdom. That God would destroy them utterly.

The word of the Lord does make an exception for the southern kingdom of Judah, prophetically telling of Jesus Christ. That there would come up on them salvation, not physically. Not as by armies and horses.

Then a son, Loammi, *for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.* This judgment is devastating, and another nail in the coffin of dispensationalism.

But even in this prophecy of destruction, the promise of the Israel of God found in Christ. That it would be said to the innumerable saints in Christ, *Ye are the sons of the living God.*

*Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land*.

teachings.title: All nations from Abraham, and his seed is Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The genealogies show the nations descend from Abraham, but the blessing is to his seed Christ, so all in Christ are heirs, and the Jews' advantage availed nothing when they rejected Him.
teachings.text:
1 Chronicles begins with clear genealogies, leading not just to David, but pointing to Christ through Mary. And also if the neighboring nations, many of whom God considered brothers of Israel, and whom are chastened and destroyed for betraying that brotherhood throughout the prophets.

It was considered outrageous when Pastor Steven Anderson laid out the case that all men alive today can trace some lineage back to Abraham, but the evidence in the Bible is clear. From Noah to Abraham, from Abraham to Ishmael, Zimran, Jokshan, Medan and Midian, and of course Isaac. And of Isaac, Esau who is Edom, and Jacob who is Israel.

All of these nations in the world descended from Abraham, and intermarried with the nations of Ham and Japheth, and spread out on the Earth.

And the blessing of Abraham's seed was to Christ, and if you be in Christ, you are of Abraham's seed, and heir to the promise. There is no Jew or Greek. All men are called.

The advantage Jews had of having the oracles of God were to no advantage, because when the time came to recognize Jesus as the Christ, they slayed Him as they had the prophets before Him.

They had Moses and the prophets and didn't believe. If one were raised from the dead, still they would not believe.

With that in mind, we enter into **1 Chronicles**.

teachings.title: The remnant of Israel and the daughter of Zion
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Zephaniah's promise to the remnant applies beyond the return from Babylon to Christ's followers and all believers in New Jerusalem, whom the false Jews of the synagogue of Satan will come to worship before.
teachings.text:
And so the prophecy given Zephaniah turns to the rebuke facing the holy city in that time. God says he will remove from there the haughty and prideful, the corrupt leaders and wicked men of Jerusalem, killed or carried away into captivity.

But, as we saw in **2 Kings**, and in **Jeremiah**, God left behind a remnant, of the poor and the afflicted. Left by Babylon to be laborers in the field. To work the vineyard. To tend to the flocks and be husbandmen to the land. And they shall trust in the name of the Lord.

*The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.*

This prophetic verse refers primarily to those left behind from the captivity, but is also talking about the believers who followed Christ in His ministry, the Apostles and disciples, and applies to the larger Christian population through the ages, and especially to those of us saved, in the resurrection, in New Jerusalem. What a wonderful picture of that glorious day.

*Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. The Lord hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy: the king of Israel, even the Lord, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more.*

These final verses are more than just the promise to return the captives from Babylon, 70 years later. It is an eternal promise to we, as believers.

Our King in the midst of us, seeing evil no more. Our transgressions gone. No fear. Working the vineyards of the Lord, His servants forevermore. He will save us, and rejoice over us. Singing songs of joy, resting in love. And

*I will gather them that are sorrowful for the solemn assembly, who are of thee, to whom the reproach of it was a burden.*

**Luke 4:14-19**
*And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.*

And the promise to make us a name among all the people of the earth, to let the unbelieving know that He has loved us, and that we are not ashamed, reminds me of Jesus prophecy in **Revelation 3:9**;

*Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.*

What a wonderful God, Who loves us so!

teachings.title: Eli's house cut off, a faithful priest raised
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The cutting off of Eli's house pictures the end of the Levitical priesthood and the old testament, replaced by Christ the High Priest and the New Testament believers as His royal priesthood.
teachings.text:
The second half of the chapter establishes the narrative of Samuel, and how, as Corban, a gift set aside for the Lord, Elkanah and Hannah gave their young son to Eli the High Priest, to be in service to the Lord.

We learn that as Samuel grew, learning the station of the Levitical priesthood he was part of, even with a linen ephod, he grew in favor with both the Lord and man.

But Eli had two sons serving at the Tabernacle, Hophni and Phinehas, who were reprobates. Sons of Belial. And they profaned the offerings brought before them, taking the choicest cuts, and demanding more of those seeking to keep the offerings of the Law. To the point where they offended many from even bothering with the sacrifices.

These reprobates even were fornicating with the women who gathered at the door of the Tabernacle, abusing their station for their own wicked lusts. And Eli knew, but did not cast them out to be stoned. He allowed them to continue in their evil ways.

And so, the Lord sent a prophet, a man of God, who preached to Eli about the evil the Lord was going to visit upon him and his house. That though God had made a promise to Aaron and his seed to be high priests, that promise was now void;

*Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people? Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed. Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father's house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house.*

The prophet continues speaking the word of God, saying;

*And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.*

This is a picture of what many professing Christians derisively call "replacement theology."

While the immediate meaning of the prophecy is found in the Lord promise to slay Hophni and Phinehas in one day, cutting off the house of Eli and giving Samuel the honor as a faithful priest, it is also a picture of the cutting off of the Levitical priesthood and the OT ceremonial laws and ordinances, and establishing Jesus as His anointed, a High Priest forever, and the NT believers as His royal priesthood.

Replacing physical Israel with the spiritual Israel. Making the Old Testament with the people null by their inability to keep their side of the deal, and so done away with by the death of Christ, and a new testament given by the shedding of His blood;

**Hebrews 9:16-22**
*For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.*

teachings.title: The land given by the election of grace
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Israel's inheritance was always conditional and by God's election of grace, and Numbers shows He casts off any branches into the fire.
teachings.text:
I will say that while the gift of the promised land was given as an inheritance to those children of Israel, by tribe and by lot, this inheritance was always not only conditional, but by the election of grace, given of God.

God elected that they would receive this land, by covenant of their keeping Him as their God, which they failed to do, the fault being with the people.

The Bible is a book of winnowing, narrowing down and casting off. Of God choosing to bless the lesser. The younger. Not by law or entitlement, but by His purpose and need. Inheritance, but with caveats to His purpose. A continuous replacement. If the study of **Numbers** has taught us anything, God has no problem casting off into the fire any branches He wishes. Reprobation in the Wilderness meant not only being damned, but destroyed in the most painful awful ways. Plague and fire and being swallowed up by the ground itself.

teachings.title: Inheritance by law, blessing by election
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Scripture throughout shows earthly inheritance by law but spiritual blessing by election, picturing the Gentiles adopted in Christ over Abraham's children after the flesh.
teachings.text:
The idea that there is a legal inheritance, for earthly matters and yet an inheritance and blessing of election for spiritual things of God, is found continuously in scripture, starting with Cain the elder, and Abel the younger. And it all pictures the adoption of the Gentiles in the seed of Abraham, who is Christ Jesus over Abraham's children after the flesh. The first children of God, circumcised of the flesh, rejected, reprobate, for the adoption of children of God, circumcised of the heart.

The entire Bible teaches this. What is derisively called "replacement theology," is simply the understanding that the eldest may receive the inheritance of earthly things, but the Kingdom of Heaven is only inherited by faith.

Just as the daughters of Manasseh were given the land promised their father in the absence of brothers by law, and Joshua was given leadership of the children of Israel by the election of faith.

teachings.title: A remnant according to the election of grace
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God has not cast away His people He foreknew, meaning the believing remnant like Paul and the seven thousand, chosen by grace and not works.
teachings.text:
Paul had just concluded that they are a disobedient and gainsaying people. God tried.

As Christ put it in **Matthew 23:37**;

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

So, what then? Are they all cut off? God forbid, for Paul is *an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.* They cannot be all cut of simply by being Israel after the flesh, or Paul wouldn't be saved.

*God has not cast away his people which he foreknew.* We have already seen that Paul has already written in **Romans 8** that those who believe, God foreknew. That same foreknowledge of believers. This is a conditional statement. It's not "God has not cast away His people," but His people that are saved.

And to make this point clear, Paul quotes Elijah, who was cursing Israel for their unbelief and seeking the prophet's life. God's reply to Elijah is that there was a remnant of Israel who were saved by faith, who had no bent the knee to Baal. Who were still faithful.

By comparing his present time to Elijah's, Paul deliberately specifies that there is a remnant, just as he himself is a remnant, according to the election of grace.

That is, a chosen people by grace, believers. Even of the Jews at that present time, as he himself is proof of.

*And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

With this aside, Paul lays the final nail in the coffin of the idea of works based salvation. The election of grace is to the glory of God, boasting excluded. Unmerited, but accessed by faith, as we have shown in earlier chapters.

teachings.title: They stumbled that the Gentiles be saved
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Israel stumbled so that Gentiles could be saved and the Jews provoked to jealousy, all revealing God's glory through His mercy and wrath.
teachings.text:
What then?

Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for.

But the election hath obtained it.

The rest were blinded.

Way back in **Romans 1** Paul firmly establishes that the Glory of God is revealed from heaven by the mercy He has shown on the believer, and His wrath on those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. That His abundant grace is shown by the forgiveness of sin, even to the Gentile, the same as with the Jew, and that forgiveness in grace reveals His glory from Heaven, so that none have any excuse.

That mercy, through us calls others to believe. That wrath on the unbelieving, calls others to believe. All to His glory.

Verse 11:11 relies on this established understanding. Have they stumbled **that** they should fall? No. God forbid. But rather they have stumbled that Gentiles be saved. Why? To provoke the unbelieving Jews to jealousy.

Because it all serves to reveal the glory of God. It's not about us. It's not about the Jews. It is about God being glorified through His grace, revealed through His mercy and wrath.

teachings.title: Provoke to emulation and save some
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Paul's wish is that by provoking his kinsmen to jealousy he might save some, conditions that dispensationalists twist into will and all.
teachings.text:
So consider this context as we read the next verse;

*Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?*

Paul says he is speaking to the Gentiles here. Asking them a question as the apostle to them; if the world is made rich in Christ because the unregenerate Jews fell, can you imagine how much more the glory of God would be revealed by their coming to believe?

Recall that Paul's still talking about his own wish, that his brethren after the flesh be saved. He has already concluded that only a remnant are, and that blindness has come on the rest. That only by being part of the election of grace, given to believers, that they can be saved and made heirs in Christ. God is not a respecter of persons. There is no Jew or Greek in Christ.

In that context, we can see Paul's wish for them expressed by the rhetorical question he asks the reader; if their fall was to bring salvation to the world, how much greater would it be if the salvation of the world brought them back?

*If by any means I may provoke to emulation then which are of my flesh, and might save some of them.*

This is the point of the jealousy God hopes to provoke in them. That some might be saved.

If...may...might...some.

Many dispensationalists will twist this series of conditions to mean "will" and "all."

teachings.title: And so all Israel shall be saved
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: All Israel in Romans 11:26 is the true seed adopted by faith, saved through Christ the Deliverer, while partial blindness remains on fleshly Israel until His coming.
teachings.text:
*For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.*

*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Here is the crux of the dispensationalist heresy. Their main proof text. "All Israel shall be saved."

But we know this is not Israel of the flesh. That not all Israel which are of Israel.

*Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel:  Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.*

And we see the conditional terms of how all Israel is saved; that a deliverer comes out of Zion, to turn away ungodliness in Jacob. Who will take away their sins.

That is Christ Jesus. The promise is made in and through Him. And so, as it is written, all Israel shall be saved.

The fullness of the Gentiles is the day of redemption. The second coming of Christ Jesus. The day of the Lord. Where the dead in Christ rise and the elect are gathered, and God's wrath is poured out in the unbelieving world.

Paul is saying that partial blindness, that veil over their hearts, is going to remain in place until the end of the world. But all Israel, the sons of God adopted by faith, who are the true seed of Abraham, shall be saved.

teachings.title: No replacement, only the covenant to all nations
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Jew and Gentile alike are saved only by faith with imputed righteousness, so there is no replacement theology and no other dispensation, only the covenant to Abraham for all nations.
teachings.text:
So, in 4 chapters we see that there is no difference between Jew and Gentile, all are under sin, all condemned, with the law or without.

We see that all who are saved from that condemnation are saved by faith in the blood of Christ Jesus. By believing God's promise. By the imputed righteousness of Jesus, our own sins are not counted against us. Without works. Not by the law. Not by circumcision. Not by being physical heirs of Abraham, but spiritual heirs in faith.

There is no replacement theology, only the continuation of the covenant made to Abraham, which is to all nations.

There was no other dispensation given. There is no future dispensation to be had.

teachings.title: Jeremiah's field: a pledge of redemption
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Jeremiah's purchase of a field during the siege promised Judah's return and, in dual fulfilment, the everlasting covenant with the Israel of God saved by faith.
teachings.text:
And so, here in **Jeremiah 32** we find the prophet held in a prison in King Zedekiah's home, as Jerusalem is besieged by the Chaldeans of Babylon. And the king is frustrated with the prophesying of spoil and desolation coming from the word of God through Jeremiah. The prediction of Judah being led to captivity, slain by sword and pestilence has left the king and those in the court in despair.

And then, the word of the Lord comes to Jeremiah the Benjaminite, and tells him of a real estate deal in the midst of a terrible siege.

It seems an unlikely thing, but the Lord instructs Jeremiah to take up the offer made to him by Hanameel, son of Shallum, the prophets uncle. A family member of the same tribe, who wishes to sell him a field in their lands, under the right of redemption. The return of lands to the people of the tribes during Jubilee.

God tells him it will happen, and it does. And he conducts the transaction according to law, witnessed and subscribed, the paperwork done. The evidences of purchase, God says to place in an earthen vessel for preservation, because this is the Lord's promise; that there will be a return. That all is not lost. A day of redemption will come and His people will have their portion of the land of milk and honey again.

And the word of the Lord tells the curse that's upon Judah, and the wickedness of the people, and the certain destruction that's upon them for their iniquities and abominations. The idols and incense burned in the house of the Lord. The high places built to Moloch, where the children of Judah pass their own children through the fire in sacrifice, something so wicked, God hadn't imagined it would be. (Men invent evil in their hearts, not commanded by God who is without sin and holy)

And having said all this, and promising the triumph of Nebuchadnezzar over them, God tells them through the prophet of His mercy. That they who are scattered and are His people will be returned again. Both the captivity, at the end of the 70 years, but in a larger sense the Israel of God. The saved and scattered nations, who shall have redemption in the land. Who shall be His people and He shall be our God.

Given one heart and one way, saved by the gospel, that we may fear Him forever, sealed by the Spirit. An everlasting covenant where God will never turn from us, the love and respect for Him, fear of the Lord, kept in our hearts that we shall not depart from Him.

In the dual fulfilment of this prophecy, God uses the transaction of the field to give hope to those with an ear to hear. That their captivity won't be forever. That men shall buy fields in the land of their fathers again, for He will cause their captivity to return. But in it, He shows us His promise to all those who are saved by faith on His word.

teachings.title: The righteous remnant and replacement theology
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: So-called replacement theology is God's will to show mercy on vessels prepared unto glory, always preserving a remnant saved by faith rather than works.
teachings.text:
Of course one of the applications we can take from this all, is that the idea of "replacement theology," really is simply understanding God's will. That He hath mercy on whom He will have mercy, and whom He will He hardeneth, *that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory*.

But there is always a righteous remnant. Those 7000 who have not bent the knee to Baal. And in who God will that His glory and mercy be seen that others may believe.

**Isaiah 1:9**
*Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.*

And it is that faith that comes from seeing His wrath on those fitted for destruction, the clay marred and discarded by the potter, and the glory of the vessels fitted for His purpose, that reveals the truth to the unbelieving that they may come to be saved by faith. Not by their own works, which is the path that led to the destruction of the Jew;

*What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone; As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.*

teachings.title: Continuation theology, not replacement theology
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Israel's broken branches and the grafting in of believers show one promise by grace through faith in the same Christ, which is why the cut-off hate us.
teachings.text:
**John 15:1-8**
 *I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned. If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.*

**Romans 11:17-25**
*And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again. For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree? For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.*

Jeremiah preaching to the Jews says; *The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.* A theme repeatedly used in scripture. And for the nation of Judah, this preaching produced the same reaction against him as it had against Jesus and the Apostles. The same reaction we get today as spiritual Israel, when we remind those who say they are Jews but are not but do lie, that we have been graft into the vine that is Christ. But they have been cut off to be burned: They threaten Jeremiah's life.

*And the Lord hath given me knowledge of it, and I know it: then thou shewedst me their doings. But I was like a lamb or an ox that is brought to the slaughter; and I knew not that they had devised devices against me, saying, Let us destroy the tree with the fruit thereof, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be no more remembered. But, O Lord of hosts, that judgest righteously, that triest the reins and the heart, let me see thy vengeance on them: for unto thee have I revealed my cause. Therefore thus saith the Lord of the men of Anathoth, that seek thy life, saying, Prophesy not in the name of the Lord, that thou die not by our hand*

They call it "replacement theology," but it is actually a continuation theology, the same promise offered by the same grace, through faith in the same Christ, the Lord Jesus.

And for this truth, they seek to kill us. Because they hated Christ first.

teachings.title: Circumcise your hearts, O Jerusalem
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God called Judah to repent with a circumcision of the heart by faith rather than of the flesh, but they were a stiff-necked people whose destruction was their own doing.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4, and the Spirit of the Lord is upon Jeremiah, preaching to the people of Judah, the children of Israel, and warning them of destruction coming from the North, the lion of Babylon. God giving the prophet visions of an invasion, all the whole the supposed prophets of the Lord are preaching "peace, peace." (As we will see in a later chapter, they are falsely telling Judah that they are fine and God loves them, but they aren't speaking for God).

The Lord tells the people to repent towards Him and He will stay His judgment. To the circumcision of the heart. Not of the flesh, the outward sign of being of the seed of Abraham, but the circumcision made without hands, of faith in the Lord.

**Romans 2:25-29**
*For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision. Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision? And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law? For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*

**Colossians 2:11**
 *In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ:*

Even as God is warning of utter destruction and the desolation of her cities, being spoiled by these invading armies, carried away into captivity, justified in His wrath, God offers His grace that if they but turn back to Him, He will repent.

*O Jerusalem, wash thine heart from wickedness, that thou mayest be saved. How long shall thy vain thoughts lodge within thee?*

We can hear in this the frustration and pleading of the Lord, longsuffering and merciful, at the end of His patience. Sorrowful and lamenting what He will do because they are a stiff-necked and gainsaying people. The same frustration Jesus felt, preaching to the Jews, 600yrs later.

**Matthew 23:37**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

God says the punishment coming is due to their own wickedness, their bitter heart. Wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge. Their destruction is their own doing, and God laments this, as a husband would putting away his wife that he loves for her adultery.

Jeremiah sees visions of desolation, cities sacked and spoiled. The sky black from smoke. The fields, destroyed. Even the birds fleeing, for there are no men left.

And the Lord, who is a jealous God, asks what will Israel do when its destruction has come? He compares the nation to an old harlot. Decked in crimson, face caked with makeup, appealing to her lovers that she fornicated with, the other nations and their gods, and He says without Him. Without their land and riches. These lovers will turn and seek their lives. Without God they are vanity.

teachings.title: The covenant kept in Christ, not in the Jews
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Leviticus 26's remedy of confession is fulfilled in Christ, and God's Israel is believers circumcised in heart, while unbelieving Jews remain under the curse.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 26** is one of the many times God reiterates the warning to Israel, that if they don't keep the conditions of the covenant God has made with them, he will curse them 7-fold, remove them from the land and set their enemies up over them.

This held specific meaning to the Hebrews in the wilderness, entering into Canaan, but it is true of all people who call themselves by His name.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

The curse against His people comes with a remedy. Because the Lord is a forgiving and merciful God.

*If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, with their trespass which they trespassed against me, and that also they have walked contrary unto me; And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity: Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.*

(Note the physical circumcision availa them nothing. It is the circumcision of the heart, made without hands, in Christ Jesus;

*In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ*.
...
*But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*)

This covenant is and always has been kept in Christ. It was to Abraham's seed, who is Jesus, and those blessings fall on those adopted into the promise by faith in Him. Those calling themselves Jews today *could* repent to be partakers of the promise, but note that they'd have to admit not only that they forsook God and didn't walk in His statutes, rejecting Christ, and deserved their punishments, but they'd have to also testify that God has walked contrary to them, and that His judgment was right.

In the various captivities and tribulations of the OT Israelites, this repentance led to their being restored. But modern Jews, so-called, maintain in their being scattered, in their being cursed, in their being kept from peace in the land, they keep the fiction that they remain God's chosen people. That they aren't being cursed for their unbelief, but that it is we who believe, those circumcised of the heart, who afflict them unjustly.

*And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.*

This is seen in the ADL and the cries of "antisemitism," seeing swastikas and threats of genocide in construction markings and preaching from the Bible. The wicked flee where none pursue. They are faint of heart, as the Lord promises.

Talmudic rabbinical Judaism shows that they despise God's statutes and abhor His judgements, so that they do not keep His commandments but instead find loopholes and rationalizations in the vain traditions of men, doctrines they invented taught as commandments of God.

His tabernacle is not set in their midst, who is Jesus. They are contrary to all men. God's wrath abides upon them to the uttermost.

God's people, Israel, has always been a nation of believers who, by faith, carry the circumcision of the heart. Today it is believing Christians, and our nations are blessed by the few within it who keep the word of God, and cursed when we who call ourselves by His name reject His judgement.

teachings.title: A remnant according to the election of grace
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Romans 11 does not make unbelieving Jews God's chosen; only a remnant elected by grace through faith is saved while the rest are blinded.
teachings.text:
And so, Paul having settled the matter regarding Israel after the flesh, that none are saved without faith in Christ, same as the Gentiles, dead under sin just as the Gentiles are, that any zeal they show towards God, without faith, is out of ignorance and going about to establish their own righteousness, all together vain; He continues stating his fervent desire that his brothers after the flesh repent, and be saved.

This chapter is abused into teaching a false doctrine that all Jews, even the modern "Jews" (who say they are Jews but do lie), are still God's chosen people and thus still are going to be saved, despite being apostate and denying Christ Jesus. They will derisively dismiss the idea that non-believing Jews are cut off and cast out, ears dulled and hearts waxen, unable to believe, as "Replacement Theology."

But the epistle to the Romans demonstrates with finality that all who don't believe are cut off, and that it is one continuation of faith that saves. The same for Jew and Greek. It isn't replacement it is continual, in the election of grace.

Old Testament Israel and New Testament Israel. Hebrew of Gentiles, all were saved by faith. The offer to the Greek came after Christ was lifted up, but it is the same offer. The same gift of eternal life in Christ through faith. Being chosen to be God's people by our belief, not by seed. Wild olive branches grafted in to the root that is found in Israel, as unbelieving Jews are cut off and burned.

Paul begins the chapter giving a rhetorical question to the conclusions he reached regarding apostate Jews in the previous chapters. *Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.* Why? Because he himself is of the Jews and a believer. So were most of the early churches. The remnant of those elect in grace, predestined in Christ (not as Calvinism teaches, but by our faith through Christ, not the other way around). If he, Paul is saved then not all of Israel is cast away. God hath not cast away his people who he foreknew. Again, those that are saved and in whom He works to make vessels fitted to His use. It is the same foreknowledge of the elect, those that would believe, not saying every Jew.

The prophet Elijah cursing Israel for their unbelief, saying "Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life," is reminded by God that He has a remnant of believers still. As wicked and apostate as Israel got, there were still 7,000 who had not bowed the knee to Baal. Paul using this to say that even then, there were Jews who believed and got saved. That all of them were not cast out.

*Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.*

The remnant is according to what? The election of grace. Which is as he already established, being saved by faith calling upon the name of the Lord. This is a conditional statement. Dispensationalism always ignores conditional statements regarding the Jews to make these things apply to all of them.

And, as an aside he makes yet another statement of salvation by faith and not of works;
*And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work*.

There is no grace if you worked for it. There is no working for it if it is of grace.

What then? If only a remnant remains of those who believed, then Israel as a nation has not obtained righteousness (they seek to establish their own), but the election in grace, believers, have obtained righteousness by faith.

And the rest were blinded. Which brings us back to chapter 1 and the reprobate doctrine. God chooses to blind those who will not believe, giving them up and giving them over.

*According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear*.

As Jesus said in **Matthew 13**, eyes closed, dull of hearing, hearts waxed gross, they cannot hear the word of God and believe.

teachings.title: Boast not against the branches
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The Gentiles are grafted into the root by grace, so they must not boast but fear, since God who cut off the natural branches could cut them off too.
teachings.text:
Continuing the thought, Paul uses a parable, a picture of what has happened, that the natural root of salvation came through Israel, and though some of those branches were broken off and burned, the Gentiles were grafted in. All by grace through faith.

And Paul warns the Gentiles not to think too highly of themselves, that it is by God's grace and to His purpose that this has happened.

We aren't naturally supposed to be there, being wild olive trees, and the tree of the vineyard that God has grown with care is pruned of the branches that aren't producing fruit, and grafted us in that will produce in an abundance, but again the glory is His.

*Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.*

We shouldn't fall to the same arrogance as the unbelieving Jews. To think we are special boys. There is no Jew or Greek in Christ. Keep humility about our situation. We all deserve Hell and Death. We are there simply by the grace and the purpose of God.

*Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.*
*Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.*

Well there means, good. Correct. You are right. The Jews were cut off that we may be grafted in. So true.

But be not high-minded, or proud, because of God did that to the nation he tended for thousands of years, He could easily do that to the Gentiles. The other nations.

teachings.title: Until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Being grafted in is conditional on faith, and the fulness of the Gentiles simply means the harvest, when the Lord reaps at His coming before the wrath.
teachings.text:
*Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again*.

Again, note the conditional statements. IF we as a people continue in belief, we will remain in His goodness, and IF the Jew in unbelief repents, they will be graft back in. It is entirely conditioned on faith.

*For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.*
