So many miss the point of this statement, which is a warning to the nations not to assume they deserve the blessings of grace through faith, as the unregenerate Jew had done. They get caught up in the "fullness of the Gentiles come in."

It is a curious turn of phrase that, because it points to a future event, many take and wrest with, trying to pinpoint what this means eschatologically. But it simply means when all those that are going to believe, have, the harvest comes. The day of the Lord, the rapture and the wrath. It's just a poetic way of saying this. Fullness being synonymous with the harvest. The fruit coming in. It isn't some esoteric hidden meaning.

Paul says that blindness *in part* (there's a remnant that believed, remember) has happened until the harvest of the nations is ready.

**Revelation 14:15**
*And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him that sat on the cloud, Thrust in thy sickle, and reap: for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe.*

God likens all of this to a vineyard throughout scripture. The spring feasts and fall feasts point to the first and second coming, the sowing and the harvest.

The fruits we produce are saved Christians we've led to Christ. The increase, the bounty of the harvest is God's. We are servants, husbandmen. He is the Lord of the harvest. And when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, He will reap.

teachings.title: The children of the flesh are not the children of God
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Romans 9 shows Israel after the flesh is cut off and the election is of the seed, Christ, not individual Calvinist election, and God has mercy on whom He will.
teachings.text:
Having established all things regarding salvation by faith, and the implications to man: believers unto righteousness found in Christ Jesus, the new man, the Spirit, and the promise of the incorruptible that comes at the redemption (as well as the sin of the flesh in the meantime), unbelief unto death, and reprobates, twice-dead, hearts hardened, Paul now moves on to addressing the Jews after the flesh, considering these settled arguments from before.

If all these things are true, and the gospel is by faith in Christ, which the prophets who came before all testified, and the law was unto death (not because of the unrighteousness of the law, but rather the infirmities of the people), and if all are under sin, Jew or Gentile, and all require faith in Christ to be saved, for there is no difference, what then?

Paul begins by expressing his sorrow that his kinsmen, the unbelieving children of Israel after the flesh are cut off. That they have had the Kingdom taken from them, as Jesus said.

*Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.*

All of these blessings, and the seed pertaining to the promise that is Christ Jesus (concerning the flesh, note the distinction, especially those "mother of God" heretics), and yet Israel are cut off.

*They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God*.

(Dispensationalists should read that again and again until it sinks in)

...*but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son. And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac*.

The promise was of the seed, the seed being Christ in the flesh, who came of the line of Jacob, born second but given the inheritance and the blessing over Esau.

**Malachi 1:2-3**
*I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.*

This is pertaining to the seed, the promise of Christ, knowing Edom would be made desolate, the election is of Jacob/Israel, that Jesus would come from Judah, the root of Jesse, from the throne of David.

This is not about individual salvation of Esau or Jacob. The election of the seed is in Christ. And it served God that the older served the younger in the promise,  in the same way that the Jew made way for the Gentile.

But the law says the older shall have the inheritance, so what then, is God unrighteous?

*God forbid. For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.*

We trust the judgment of God. Who knows beginning from end. That all are chosen in Christ, not unto belief. Not given faith by God, but predestined in Christ to be given the blessing, the promise and the inheritance, to all who believe.

And so God, in His wisdom, shows mercy to who He will show mercy. And compassion on whom He will.

And harden the hearts of those fitted for destruction. All to His glory. Because as we have established; the righteousness of God is revealed both in His mercy towards us, and the love that gave His only begotten Son for us, but in His wrath against those who hold the truth in unrighteousness.

teachings.title: All Israel saved in Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Unbelieving Jews were made reprobate like Pharaoh while a believing remnant remains, since all God's promises are kept in Christ the one seed.
teachings.text:
And so, as Paul in the Spirit testifies, he wishes that his brothers after the flesh would come to the faith. But they are cut off. Just as Esau become Edom, and they were made desolate, Jews were cut off and consumed.

Is God's judgment unrighteous? No. Is His word unfaithful? Again no, for a remnant remains, those saved by faith as is Paul, and to believing Jews whom he writes to in Rome. But the unbelieving Jew, hearts hardened, had their chance, and their destruction served to show the glory of God.

*For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.*

Just as Pharaoh was made reprobate, so too are the Jews after the flesh.

God's promises were kept in Christ. The remnant is in Christ. All Israel was saved, in Christ. The Kingdom, the land that was promised, is through Christ. The blessings were to the seed, and that seed is singular; Christ.

teachings.title: The entire Bible teaches one faith in Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: What is mocked as replacement theology is simply the Bible's one theme of salvation in Christ from Moses to Revelation, which dispensationalism denies.
teachings.text:
The entire Bible teaches what is derisively called replacement theology. Better phrased; The entire Bible teaches the one faith of salvation and redemption in Christ. The failure of man in the flesh to find holiness in the works of their own righteousness, and the grace and mercy of God in providing a sacrifice for their sin that they may know Him. For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life.

Moses wrote of Jesus, in Genesis. In Exodus. In Leviticus and Deuteronomy. The prophets spoke of Him, and preached His gospel of redemption and reconciliation. The Psalms sing of Him and His coming. Jesus Christ in the flesh spent 3.5 years of an earthly ministry reaching the lost sheep of Israel that He could lead who were His, calling them to repentance and preaching to the unbelieving that they were going to be replaced and cast into outer darkness with wailing and gnashing of teeth.

Once the veil is torn at the death of Christ, the remaining scripture teaches of the gospel given to a people who were not a nation, now heirs to the Kingdom. The branches that did not produce fruit meet for repentance, cast into the fire.

The epistles giving us the grafting in, the theology of salvation and religion undefiled. The Revelation of Christ Jesus, the rapture of believers, the resurrection, adoption and redemption God predestined in His Son. And God's final judgement that we may know it, and come to Him before it's too late.

And it is this simple truth, the entire theme of scripture, that the false doctrine of dispensationalism denies and rejects.

teachings.title: If ye will obey, a peculiar treasure
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The Sinai covenant was conditional and Israel broke it, so it was replaced by the new covenant and those saved in Christ are now God's peculiar people, refuting dispensational Zionism.
teachings.text:
IF *ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine.*

This is the foundation of the covenant at Sinai, the promise made to the children of Israel by God, that IF they kept it, they would be a peculiar people, special to God.

God judges nations on earth by their works. He judges people as individuals by their faith. His promises to nations are conditional. They are if/then. To us as individual souls, the only condition to be His is faith in Christ.

The if/then covenant with Israel, that they broke themselves repeatedly, despite God's longsuffering and mercy, despite being given chance after chance to get right, they broke entirely with the Crucifixion, the rejection of His Son Jesus. But it is in Jesus that are made partakers of the new and better covenant. The better testament. And the old one is done away with.

*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.*

And where was the fault of the first? In the Israelites.

*For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.*

This is the bookend to the Sinai covenant, fulfilled:
*I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

And this should be the final nail in the coffin for the Dispensationalist Zionist heresy that God is still on the hook for the first covenant. No, He has replaced the physical nation with a new one. Israel was to be a peculiar people, but failed. Now His peculiar people are those saved in Christ.

*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.*

teachings.title: The vineyard given to others
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: In the parable of the husbandmen God takes the vineyard of His covenant from the unfruitful Jewish leaders and gives it to others, the replacement theology found throughout the Bible.
teachings.text:
It's important to point out and interesting to consider that the same authority who ordained John's baptism, Who sent the prophets and beloved Son, Is the same authority who put these husbandmen in charge. God the Father. Jehovah LORD.

And the vineyard, being His covenant, and the fruit thereof His people, Jesus telling them that they are rebellious to the authority that they question of Christ, that they will have the vineyard, the care of that covenant, taken from them and given to others.

To which they react, "God forbid!"

This is what is called today. Replacement Theology. This idea that the vineyard has been given to others, to be overseen by other people, Who aren't the Jews. Who aren't the Levitical priesthood. Who aren't the scribes and lawyers and Pharisees and Sadducees, the elders who were unfruitful. The rebellious husbandmen, these unfruitful vine are cut off and burned.

The covenant given to another people. A New Testament.

The idea of replacement theology is found throughout the Bible. It is not some newfound doctrine, it isn't some Paulian heresy. It is the will of God the Father.

It is just. It is righteous. It has happened.

And all those who deny it, who defend these rebellious husbandmen, let them be accursed for rejecting the judgment of God and defending the murderers of Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: The Key of David Opens and Shuts
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Christ opens the door of salvation that none can shut and also shuts in reprobation, and those who say they are Jews but deny Christ are liars, spiritually Edom.
teachings.text:
*And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;*

Jesus addresses the church at Philadelphia. Jesus is holy and true. He has the key of David, mentioned in **Isaiah 22:22**:

*And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.*

To Him gave all the prophets witness.

Also, don't miss this, Jesus opens the door of salvation to us as individual believers, and none may shut it. We have eternal life. It can't be lost or taken. But Christ Jesus also has the ability to shut the door, that none may open. This is reprobation, and it's a doctrine found throughout the Bible. Many find it difficult to accept or believe, but it is taught throughout scripture, clearly and with examples. Sadly today, many are offended at the concept.

Jesus continues, praising them for their faith. Promising He's opened the door for them. Man has little strength. We cannot open that door ourselves, only His may.

*I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.*

The church in Philadelphia is being persecuted, like some of the others, and again it is the Jews. Jesus says they say they are Jews but are not. That they are liars.

There are theories and interpretations as to what this means. Edomites? The Ashkenazi? Khazarians? These are earthly interpretations, with physical/genetic/ethnic implications. And they may very well be a marker that has some application. But what we know for certain, spiritually, that they who say they are Jews but are not, are spiritually Edom indeed. They are Esau, who sold their birthright, which has been taken by the Gentiles who are spiritually Jacob.

**Romans 2:28-29**
*For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*

For us, it is sufficient to understand that those who reject the Son have not the Father. That those who deny Jesus is the Christ are liars, and antichrists. By focusing on the spiritual application, it becomes inarguable that they who say they are Jews are not, but are liars. Without going down rabbi holes arguing about their origins and debates about genealogies. The word of God is sharper than any arguments of man, and discerns quickly exactly why they are not Jews; for if they kept the law of Moses and believed the prophets, they would believe Jesus is who He says He is. That He is the Christ.

But we who are spiritually His, who are inwardly circumcised of the heart, we can take solace in our tribulations caused by the wicked Jew antichrists, that they are a synagogue of Satan and Jesus will make them worship at His feet and know that He loves us, His brothers and sisters who believed on His name. Who trusted God's word.

Every knee shall bow and every tongue confess. Amen!

Continuing to the Philadelphians;
*Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth. Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.*

Jesus encourages them. They are doing well. Holdfast. Faint not. And as the temptation, the test of the deceiver, comes upon the world, they who remain patient and true will be protected from the deception. Note that Jesus encourages them to maintain their works and faith that they not lose crowns. Crowns are rewards in Heaven given to believers based on our works.

teachings.title: Jews Falsely So-Called Are Spiritually Edom
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: There is no ethnic role in salvation, so the Jews who reject Christ are spiritually Edom while believers are spiritually Israel heirs of a better country.
teachings.text:
In the end, we are told by history, when there was a rebellion against Rome in 70AD, it included the ethnic line of Judah. The remnants of Benjamin and Levi. And whatever Edomites who remained. All constituted what became known collectively as Jews. And, according to the history, all were wiped out and scattered abroad, forbidden by Rome to return to Judea.

Much speculation has risen out of these events and about these people. It is a rabbi hole that can be fascinating to go down, but what matters really is what God's word clearly says.

We can't know anything else for certain, as it becomes arguing genealogies and Jewish fables.

What I believe is that, because there is no genetic or ethnic role in salvation, that it is individual souls that are saved, that flesh profiteth nothing, that to here is neither Jew nor Greek, pursuit of the racial lines of Edom and Jews, the tribes of Israelites, etc, should really only be looked at in a carnal, earthly way. A fun pass time. Something to wonder about in our idleness. Spiritually, whatever happened to them is irrelevant.

We know Jews, falsely so-called, Synagogue of Satan, those who say they are Jews but are not, are spiritually Edom. Regardless of what Kaiser Sose origin story they muddy the waters with.

They were taken out of the physical promised land for rejection of Christ. Whatever claim they had to the promise ended with the fulfilment of the blessing, which is in Jesus.

And if the Jews who are spiritually Edom, who sold their birthright and blessing for earthly things, are actual sons of Esau, who is Edom, seeking to steal back the birthright Jacob took, it doesn't change anything for us who are spiritually Israel.

We know they are antichrists. We know the Gospel is the truth. We look forward to a better country, a kingdom we are inheritors of through God's grace and mercy, in Christ. Let them squabble over dessert sand. Let them persecute us in Jesus' name. We have already overcome.

teachings.title: If ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Abraham's blessing passed to Isaac and is fulfilled in Christ, so all believers are Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise.
teachings.text:
Abraham was 175 when he died. He was 137 when Sarah died, and here it says he remarried and had at least 6 sons with Keturah, and they begat many sons, but the physical inheritance and the spiritual blessing, given Abraham by God concerning Jesus, Abraham passes down to Isaac. The child of faith.

*And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.*

*Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.*

*And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre; The field which Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth: there was Abraham buried, and Sarah his wife.*

Abraham died and was gathered to his people, in heaven. It couldn't be into his own "bosom" after all. But the patriarch is given an end of days and an account of his death, which the Bible uses to signify the humanity of the fathers and the prophets.

Christ Jesus comments on the faith of Abraham and his joy at the fulfillment of the promise made to him in **John 8**;

 *Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad.*..*Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.*

And so it was that Abraham's seed was a blessing to the whole world, especially of those who believe.

**Galatians 3**

*For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*

*There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

Let this comfort you who believe, and drive to envy those of you still on the fence, trusting your own righteousness to provide your own salvation, bringing you to repent. Knowing Abraham trusted God and obtained the righteousness of Christ, and so to do we. For God is not slack concerning His promises. And we who are of Abraham's seed in Christ Jesus are joint heirs with Him. Rejoice!

teachings.title: Circumcision of the heart
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Abraham's circumcision pictured the circumcision of the heart by the Spirit, for a true Jew is one inwardly.
teachings.text:
Now, Abram becomes Abraham, decades after his salvation by calling upon the name of the Lord, and is given the physical sign of the covenant, circumcision of the flesh.

Of course, this physical act of obedience was a picture of the sealing a soul by the Holy Spirit to come. The circumcision of the heart.

**Romans 2**
*28 For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:*

*29 But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God*

**Colossians 2:11**
*In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ:*

For while the descendants of Abraham kept the circumcision as an ordinance to remember their covenant with God that brought about Christ Jesus in the flesh, to preserve the seed, even as strangers and bondsmen were added to the nation, in case any forgot God's promise, the circumcision of the heart which is found in believers is to us who are saved a reminder of our salvation and belonging to the body of Christ.

teachings.title: Thy seed as the stars: one promise, one faith
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The promise of seed as the stars is fulfilled in Christ and the innumerable redeemed of Revelation 7, not the modern Jew, under one faith in both testaments.
teachings.text:
The word of God came to Abram in a vision.

**John 1:1-2**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God*.

The Bible tells us who the word of God is. It is Jesus.

*Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.*

Abram, old when he called upon the name of the Lord and received blessings and promises, now even older and without a true heir, questions the Lord. *Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.* Abram's faith tested, the word of God says to him: *This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.*

We see in scripture that this promise was kept, his seed being one, Jesus Christ. And in Him the promise of a nation innumerable, like the stars in the sky, is fulfilled in **Revelation 7**. That following the tribulation and the rapture, there are saints, redeemed in the blood of Christ. 144,000 Old Testament saints, 12,000 from each of the tribes listed (not Jews, but Israelites) and; *A great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues.*

This is the promise to Abraham. Not for the modern Jew. Not for the apostate and wicked modern state calling itself Israel. But of Christ and Him crucified, with the power to make the elect heirs to the Kingdom of Heaven; whosoever will call upon the name of the Lord.

Old Testament. New Testament. The same dispensation. The same promise. The same faith.

teachings.title: To thy seed, which is Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The promises to Abraham's seed are fulfilled in Christ, in whom believers inherit the land forever, while Lot pitching his tent toward Sodom warns against choosing worldly ease.
teachings.text:
Chapter 13 of Genesis brings Abram and Sarai and his nephew Lot back to the land of Canaan, back to where Abram called upon the name of the Lord, near Bethel, which is on the West bank of the Jordan, in the area of Jerusalem and Bethlehem. There, scripture reminds us, he had built an altar.

Because of the greatness of his herds and Lot's, and growing contentions between each other's herdsmen, he gives Lot a choice of grazing land, and Lot chooses the area around the plains of the Jordan, just above what's called the Dead Sea today.

Given the choice, and seeing there was much water and vegetation, *even as the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt.* And so enticed, he pitches his tent there to the east, towards Sodom. There's many times in life we are given a choice like this, and choosing from ease or greed or comfort, we pitch our tents towards Sodom, towards wickedness and sin. There's a spiritual application there.

Abram, meanwhile, settles down to Hebron and the plains of Mamre. And God gives Abram two more promises, *all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever,* and *I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth,* too numerous to count.

The Bible says in **Galatians 3:16**

*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.*

Christ is the answer to the promises, kept by God. Jesus is the seed through whom all nations are blessed. It is in Jesus that the promised land is given forever, to those who believe and call upon the name of the Lord. It is in this seed that Abram can be said to have fathered a people too numerous to count, saved sons of God.

*Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the* Lord*.*

teachings.title: The mystery: Gentiles are fellowheirs
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The mystery revealed to Paul is that Gentiles are fellowheirs in Christ, under the same dispensation of grace given to all men since Adam, not a separate one.
teachings.text:
For the cause of the good news, that all who believe are joint heirs, in Christ, Paul is writing as a prisoner. In chains, under tribulation, but free in Christ, he wants the Gentiles reading this epistle to understand the depths of his devotion towards the ministry unto them that he has received from God. A dispensation of grace given unto the Gentiles as it already had been to the Jews, in faith through Christ.

What had in times past been a mystery. How God would achieve the promise of all nations being blessed in Abraham's seed, Jesus. Now Paul understands the mystery and is explaining it to them.

That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body and partakers of His promise, in Christ by the Gospel.

Paul's mission is to reveal the answer to this mystery, to proclaim the good news. To make all men see.

This dispensation of grace is being extended to all, is not a different dispensation as some would claim, but the same as given the Israelites, and all men, from Adam. Since Seth and his sons called upon the name of the Lord. All who bow their knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named.

We are a holy and separate people, called by His name.

And as such, with Christ dwelling in our hearts by faith, we are able to know the breadth, length, depth, and height of all the bounty of blessings made available to God's children. Amen.

teachings.title: Abraham's seed is Christ, and believers are heirs
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Believing Gentiles are Abraham's children through Christ the one seed, the law was a schoolmaster and not a separate dispensation, and no Jew, Rome or church can annul or add to God's covenant of faith.
teachings.text:
Paul asks the supposedly saved Christians of Galatia, *Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?* The answer is obvious to those that have the Spirit inside them, testifying to its truth. But to those still believing on their own righteousness to redeem them, this question is vexing indeed.

Quoting scripture regarding Abraham, who the Bible says in **Genesis 15:6** *And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.* This proof of our faith in God's promise of Christ Jesus being what is counted for righteousness is also quoted by Paul in **Romans 4** and in **James 2** (although to much consternation to those trusting their works to save them).

Paul reminds the Galatians that just because Jews come to tell them they need to add works of the law to their faith for salvation, that they hold no special place. That the Gentiles who received the same faith as Abraham are sons of Abraham, that all nations are blessed by Abraham's seed, that is Christ. Not seeds, plural, as in Jews after the flesh.

This chapter is also one of many nails in the coffin of dispensationalism, that wicked and often damnable heresy that places Jews in a higher regard than those that believe on Christ. The lie that they had a different way to be justified. Paul calls what they claim as a blessing, a curse.

The law was a school master, bringing those who lived under it to the understanding that no man can be justified by the works of the law. To remind them to keep the faith in the promise of God, rather than themselves. It was designed to bring them to faith, not a separate dispensation.

And of that covenant of faith, and the good news of it, no man may disannul or add to it. Read that part carefully. Understand what it means.

God made a contract with us. It is the promise of being made heirs to the Kingdom and the blessings that go along with being heirs. Being His sons. That promise only requires believing on Him to deliver on it.

Those who say they can take away your role in the promised kingdom, or adding requirements to receive it, who seek to annul or add to the covenant of God given in his testament, are liars. They can't.

Jews, Catholic church, the daughters of it, etc...cannot take away your salvation or add obedience to their traditions to receive the inheritance of faith given to Abraham, and promised by God to whosever believe. It isn't possible. They have no authority to change a covenant, a contract, given by God.

Paul says the law given to the Hebrews through Moses by God Himself didn't have the power to disannul the covenant He made with Abraham. Imagine having the hubris to think some institution of man could!

The law wasn't given to give life, but to condemn so we could understand we needed righteousness by faith.

Scripture says that God made a promise to Abraham, that faith in that promise justifies, that justification by the law is only possible by obeying the whole of it, that this is impossible, that if we place our faith in our ability to do the whole of the law, we becomes slaves to it, and that we all fall short, making the law a curse. But that in grace, we are saved by faith in Christ. Summarized:

*But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.*

And if we believe?

.*.ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.*
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*
*There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

teachings.title: Stiffnecked and resisting the Holy Ghost
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Stephen's history shows Israel's constant rejection of God, so a chosen race outside Christ is fiction; God's theology never changed, only who receives His grace.
teachings.text:
The history of the Israelites, given by Stephen, which had been preached about by prophets before, by John the Baptist and by Christ Jesus, and that would be repeated in the Epistles, is a searing indictment of them as a people, and of man in general.

God pounds the message of their stiff-neckedness and disobedience, their rejection of His word, over and over again throughout the Bible. The idea of their being special or chosen as a race, outside of Christ, is unbiblical fiction. The idea of separate ethnic dispensations is a lie. "Replacement theology" itself is a misnomer, as the theology of God in scripture has remained consistent throughout, it is simply who has received the grace of God and His blessing that's changed.

teachings.title: Romans 9: the Jews stumbled at faith
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Romans 9 is about God using nations and the unbelieving Jews' standing, not Calvinist election, and the Jews missed the promise because they sought righteousness by the law, not faith.
teachings.text:
Here Paul begins dealing with the JQ. While Calvinism uses these verses, which are about the use of nations, rulers, sinners and believers to His purpose, as being about our salvation, they do so ignoring the scriptural, Spiritual arguments that have been building throughout the epistle.

Having established God's word, His grace, our faith, the doctrine of Christ and the condition of the saved being heirs to the promise, adopted sons, he turns to explaining the unrepentant Jew's position with God, relative to the old covenant and salvation in Christ. Replacement theology is the theme. Dispies hate this.

Note what the stumblingstone preventing the Jews from being partakers of the promise; faith. They seek righteousness by the works of the law, not faith.

But WHOSOEVER believeth on Jesus Christ shall not be ashamed for trusting God's promise.

teachings.title: The promise was to Abraham's seed, which is Christ
teachings.summary: The promise to Abraham was made to his seed Christ and to all who are in Christ, the land promise was fulfilled under Joshua and kept conditionally under the Mosaic covenant, so Zionism wrongly gives the inheritance to unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 48** broadly captures the grandeur and love of God towards His holy land. This love is seen long before Israel as a nation enters in, or even exists. It was in the beginning, when God promised a land to Abraham.

**Genesis 12:1–3**
*Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.*

The promise to Abraham was both for the land, and the Christ. Long before the exodus. Long before the wandering. Before Isaac was ever born, the land that would become Israel, the province of Judah, the city of Jerusalem, in the mountains of Zion, was set apart for God.

The blessings and inheritance made to Abraham, who believed God and it was counted for righteousness, was made to him and his seed. Jesus Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.*

Zionism is a modern political ideology that takes the promise to Abraham, and rather than give the inheritance and blessing to Christ, and all who are in Christ, gives it to unbelieving, apostate Jews.

**Galatians 3:27–29**
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The claim for the children of Israel to the land, by promise of God, was fulfilled in the time of Joshua.

**Joshua 21:43–45**
*And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein. And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand. There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.*

The promise to Abraham was unconditional. But the promise made to Moses by God in the wilderness, for His people to occupy His land, was conditional.

**Deuteronomy 28:63–64**
*And it shall come to pass, that as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you; so the LORD will rejoice over you to destroy you, and to bring you to nought; and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it. And the LORD shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.*

Many Christians today will say "God keeps His promises! The Jews deserve this land!" They place political Zionism and the ethnic ultranationalism of the modern Jewish state as being part of an unconditional and irrevocable covenant with the people by heritage and genealogy.

But the Bible is clear, that the covenant made in the wilderness was explicitly conditional, that what was given to the people through Moses could not, by their failure, disannul the promise made to Abraham and his singular seed.

**Galatians 3:17–18**
*And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect. For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.*

But the covenant made those 430 years after Abraham? It has faded away, replace by a better covenant with better promises, to all who are in Christ, regardless of their ethnicity or origin.

teachings.title: God is no respecter of persons
teachings.summary: Jewish ethnic supremacy is wicked since God is no respecter of persons; He judges individuals by faith and nations by works and always offered His blessing to any who trusted Him.
teachings.text:
*The LORD looketh from heaven; he beholdeth all the sons of men. From the place of his habitation he looketh upon all the inhabitants of the earth. He fashioneth their hearts alike; he considereth all their works.*

We are all the same in His eyes. We are all guilty before Him, convicted in sin. All are in need of a savior.

The modern form of Jewish ethnic supremacy, a concept that as God's chosen people, it is because of their own qualities and holiness, is wicked. God is not a respecter of persons.

He judges individuals by faith and nations by works. And the offer to give His blessings to any king who chose to place their trust in Him, rather than strength of horses and size of armies, was always extended.

Nineveh was spared by their faith, believing the reluctant prophet Jonah. King Nebuchadnezzar's humbling 7 years in the wilderness struck with madness, led to him proclaiming the truth of God to the world. The Queen of the South came to Solomon in order to understand the truth of God.

*Behold, the eye of the LORD is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy; To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.* Whosoever will come, He shall deliver.

And so we sing.

*Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield. For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we hope in thee.*

Amen!

teachings.title: Nehemiah's gathering was conditional on repentance
teachings.summary: Nehemiah's prayer shows gathering depended on turning to God, so modern Israel, born of pride and unbelief, is not a fulfillment.
teachings.text:
We are in **Nehemiah 1**, which continues the narrative of the rebuilding of Jerusalem, and it picks up roughly 13 years after the end of Ezra. Nearly 100yrs after Haggai and Zechariah.

And we are told that the city's walls and gate remain in ruin, still fire scorched from the original invasion by Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian empire.

Nehemiah, the cup bearer to the Persian king Artaxerxes I, in the 10th year of his reign, laments the languished reconstruction. That now, after many divine starts and human stops, Jerusalem still is not walled.

He recounts the instructions of Moses, that if the people who call themselves the children of Israel failed to keep God's commandments, and chase after other gods, they would be scattered to the ends of the earth.

But if they turn back again to Him, repenting towards the God of their fathers, He will bless them and gather them again.

Nehemiah's prayer is often used by dispensationalists, saying "See, this proves that God will always gather His people!"

But, alas, this is the final time. The city God chose to place His name needs to be ready for the coming of the Messiah. The people have been unable and unwilling to repent. Only a remnant remain faithful.

In a few centuries, Jerusalem will be under Roman control which will act as a means to protect and preserve the city until Jesus' birth. Doing what the Jews failed to do all this time.

Also, we see Nehemiah lay out the condition for this gathering, that the people turn back to the Lord and obey Him. That includes being ready for the coming of Christ, with hearts ready. That if they believed Moses and the prophets, they would be prepared for Him.

Modern Israel was not the result of Jews coming to repentance, and turning towards God the Father by embracing His Son. It was the result of pride, and satanic forces. They are cut off in unbelief, their covenant faded away.

As Jesus cried;  *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

*Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.*

teachings.title: The dry bones are the resurrection, not 1948
teachings.summary: The valley of dry bones prophesies the literal resurrection and Christ's kingdom over the Israel of God, and dispensationalists wickedly give these promises to unbelieving Jews by applying them to 1948.
teachings.text:
We are in **Ezekiel 37**, perhaps the most well known passage in the prophetic book, and the preaching of the valley of dry bones.

Them bones, them bones, them dry bones.

It is one of the clearest prophecies of the resurrection and millennial kingdom of believers in the Old Testament. In the second part of the chapter, He has the prophet show two sticks to the people, one Judah, the other Ephraim, or Israel, the Northern Kingdom, and they are miraculously joined in the prophet's hand.

*Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel. And ye shall know that I am the Lord, when I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves, And shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live*.

Not only shall the graves give up their dead, and risen bodies be made whole, and the winds from the four corners give life, but God says He *shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live*, and be ruled over as one nation, the Israel of God, under *David, my servant* - Christ Jesus.

Many dispensationalists today will claim this is a prophecy for "the Jews." God says no, He will gather all the people to their land.

They will say this was fulfilled in 1948. John Hagee and Hal Lindsey and other famous dispensationalist Zionists have pushed this idea, repeatedly in their efforts to pervert Christian judgment regarding the modern state claiming to be Israel.

They teach that **Ezekiel 37** and the valley of dry bones prophecy refers to the restoration of Israel in 1948, and falsely interprets the vision as a symbolic representation of the "Jewish people's return to their land after centuries of exile." In this view, the dry bones coming to life signify the physical and national rebirth of Israel, with the reestablishment of the state in 1948 seen as a fulfillment of "God's promise."

One of the most wicked aspects of dispensationalism is that it gives holy promises to believers to unbelieving Jews. It makes firm promises into vague and dark sayings, to justify their false teachings.

The literal resurrection is promised. The Spirit of God indwelling us. The Kingdom of Christ, ruled by Jesus.

Not godless antichrists, who reject Him.

We will be joined as one Kingdom, the Israel of God, made up of believers from Adam through the final Christian saved before the day of the Lord comes. This is a promise to those of us in the New Testament, as much as it was to believers in Ezekiel's day. Amen

teachings.title: The new heart promise fulfilled in Christ, not 1948
teachings.summary: The promise of a new heart and new covenant in Ezekiel 36 is fulfilled in Christ for the Israel of God, not in the UN-created state of unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
The second half of **Ezekiel 36** drifts into end times prophecy. A new promise, which we have seen made elsewhere, where He will give a new heart, and a new spirit within the people, and His Spirit within, and cause us by the law in our hearts to walk in His statutes, and to keep His commandments. To dwell in the land of the fathers. *And ye shall be My people, and I will be your God*.

**Jeremiah 31:31-34**
*Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they brake, although I was an husband unto them, saith the Lord: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people. And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the Lord: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.*

**Hebrews 10:16-17**
*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

This promise is fulfilled in Christ.

This is not fulfilled by the UN creating the modern state of Israel. They have not gotten a new heart. They have not accepted Christ. Their desolation has not become like the garden of Eden. They are not ashamed and confounded, remembering their sin, loathing themselves for their iniquity.

This promise of restoration is done to the Israel of God, both OT and NT believers, in the end times.

 Not unbelieving Jews today.

teachings.title: We have Abraham to our father
teachings.summary: The claim that the Jews inherit the land as Abraham's many children is the false basis of Zionism, since the promises were always conditional on obedience to God's covenant.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 33** concludes, the destruction of Jerusalem has happened. One who escaped comes to the prophet in the evening and tells him, but the hand of God keeps Ezekiel from responding until the morning came, and he was no longer struck dumb. And he receives the word of God.

The Lord says that those from the wastes and wilderness of Judah, who escaped out of the desolation of Jerusalem speak, saying that because Abraham was one, and was promised land, that they being many deserve the inheritance.

This is the argument made by Jews today. The basis of Zionism. The false doctrine that because they are children of the law, and many, the promise of the land given Abraham should apply even more so to them.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

The promises and inheritance was never given a people because of who they were. But by the condition of what they did. A condition repeatedly given.

**Exodus 19:5**
*Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine*

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The word of the Lord upon Ezekiel stresses these same points. They are filled with violence and Idolatry and adultery and abominations.

For this, God says He will lay the land most desolate because of their abominations. Then they shall know He is the Lord.

teachings.title: The Jews were never the heroes
teachings.summary: The prophets show the Jews were always a stiff-necked, rebellious people under God's curse, against the Zionist view that they remain His chosen.
teachings.text:
The current debates over the role of modern Israel, Zionism and dispensationalism in Christianity rests on the idea that the Jews are and always have been God's chosen people. His elect by the law and the covenant. That He would always bless Israel.

The false understanding many professing Christians have is that in the Old Testament, Jews were the heroes of the story. That while they had their faults, God never rejected them, and in the New Testament, other than some of their leaders, they still were God's chosen, and so someday, all physical Israel would be saved.

It is impossible to read the prophets and come away with the idea that the Jews are generally the good guys. They were always a stiff-necked rebellious people who needed to be punished to do right, and even then rarely repented.

Full of complaints. Full of formication and adultery. From Egypt through Babylonian captivity, and beyond. They were continually cursed and spoken against by the word of God.

teachings.title: The promise is to the faithful
teachings.summary: The regathering promise of Ezekiel 11 is to the faithful, not to every Jew, as dispensationalists claim.
teachings.text:
The present vision of Jerusalem given to Ezekiel by the glory of the Lord concludes. Here, the prophet is shown the East Gate, and 25 men, princes of the people. Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah among them.

The Lord says these men devise mischief and give wicked counsel. They tell everyone that they are safe, as safe as meat in a pot. Flesh in a caldron. So build houses, make plans, settle in. It's all going to be ok. But the Lord has other plans.

Because of the murder and violence on the city, and the blood of the slain, He says He will bring them out of the city, even to the borders of the country and the sword shall fall on them. And they shall know He is the Lord.

And as Ezekiel prophesied, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died.

The reality of the revelation of the Lord comes upon Ezekiel, and he cries for his people, asking if the Lord shall wipe all of them out, making a full end of the remnant of Israel.

God says that He has cast them out of the land because of their presumption that they are entitled to us, absent faith in the Lord.

He says that, in their diaspora, He will be as a little sanctuary for them in the lands He scatters them to, and that He will gather them again, that they take away the abominations, the idols and rejection of God.

Dispensationalists love the next part;
*Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God; I will even gather you from the people, and assemble you out of the countries where ye have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel. And they shall come thither, and they shall take away all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof from thence. And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh: That they may walk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.*

But they fail to recognize that this is a promise to the faithful, the righteous by faith, not for every one.

*But as for them whose heart walketh after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their way upon their own heads, saith the Lord God.*

God's promises are always for the faithful. Without faith, it is impossible to please God.

teachings.title: The temple mount debate doesn't matter
teachings.summary: Which hill the temple stood on does not matter, and any third temple will not be God's; Jerusalem is the Lord's and He will repay.
teachings.text:
There have been arguments lately about what hill in Jerusalem is the correct spot for the Temple. Foolish debate, because it doesn't matter. Zion, Mt. Moriah, Jerusalem is the place, from Melchizedek, to Abraham bringing Issac to be sacrificed, to the crucifixion of Jesus, and His resurrection.

What unbelieving Jews and Muslims do there doesn't matter. If a so-called 3rd temple is built, it won't be God's. If the Man of Perdition lays siege and slaughters the Jews in days of vengeance, and sits in the place of God declaring himself God, it won't matter. Because it is the Lord's and He will repay. It will be as a crown to Him. A holy bride. Amen.

teachings.title: God is through with the Jews
teachings.summary: The return of Judah's remnant was needed only for the promise of Christ, so there is no end-times promise for the Jews as a people apart from individual faith in Jesus.
teachings.text:
Dispensationalists will point to verses about the remnant of Judah returning to Jerusalem after Babylonian captivity to draw parallel to the end times, and say that there's a similar promise for the end times. The only issue is that, while God had need is the seed of David and the city of Jerusalem, to fulfill the promise of Christ, there's no such need in the New Testament.

The only things we can point to is the likelihood of there being a third temple built for the Antichrist to declare himself God in, and the promise of days of vengeance against those who say they are Jews, but are not and do lie. That Jesus will make them know He loves us. God regards them no more. Unless their unbelief changes, individually coming to Jesus, God is through with the Jews.

teachings.title: Spared for David's sake and Jerusalem's
teachings.summary: Judah was spared only for God's promise to David and for Jerusalem, pointing to Christ, not for the sake of the Jews.
teachings.text:
Amos preaches against Jerusalem, Zion, where they feel safe in their sins compared to the North. Their wealth and palaces hated by God.

The Lord describes their land as better than any in all Assyria, or of the Philistines. Their riches and excess in food. Their luxury of being able to work on music and new instruments, comfortable beds, drinking wine out of bowls. He promised their destruction.

Tearing down the great houses. Killing the princess there. Captivity and affliction. They aren't going to escape His judgement.

It is important to keep in mind that God only kept Judah from being utterly destroyed like the rest of Israel, for two reasons; His promise to David that Jesus would come from his line, and the city Jerusalem, where He chose to place His name.

People who place the importance of Jerusalem on the Jews who occupy it, that Judah was spared destruction for their sakes', somehow, aren't rightly dividing the word. It is plain and clear:

**1 Kings 11:32**
*But he shall have one tribe for my servant David's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel*.

This explanation is given by God repeatedly, leading up to the judgment against Israel and the Babylonian captivity, and it only makes sense in the context of Christ Jesus.

**Isaiah 1:9**
*Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah*.

That remnant includes the 14 generations from David to Jesus.

teachings.title: Shouldest thou help the ungodly?
teachings.summary: God's wrath on Jehoshaphat for helping Ahab condemns Christian Zionism today, which calls unbelieving Jews who curse Christ our greatest allies.
teachings.text:
In the matter of Ahab, and Jehosaphat's allegiance with the northern kingdom of Israel, the word of the Lord came upon the prophet Jehu.

*Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord.*

Being yoked to the wicked, even your own brothers after the flesh, which is what Jehosaphat used to justify it, does not please God.

How much more then the Zionism of many Christians today? If God's wrath is upon unbelieving Jews to the uttermost, how much more those that place them as our "greatest allies?" People who should know better, whom God's word is the final authority, and yet they join light for darkness. Blessing antichrists who curse the holy name of Jesus.

teachings.title: Howbeit they did not hearken: the if/then covenant
teachings.summary: Dispensationalists ignore that God's covenant with Israel was conditional, and He destroyed Israel when they would not hearken, a lesson for modern Israel.
teachings.text:
Dispensationalists and modern Jews will always ignore the if/then nature of the covenant with the children of Israel, the promise to be their God and they to be His people, so long as they walked in His statutes and kept the fear of the Lord. They ignore the destruction of Israel found here in this chapter. They ignore the warnings given of the prophets that spike against the sin of Israel. They ignored the famines and the plagues and invasions and spoiling by their enemies. They forgot about the bounty and blessings and impossible victories given to their fathers.

*Howbeit they did not hearken*...

And the Lord, longsuffering and merciful, finally has enough, and destroys them.

The country of Samaria is filled with outlandish people, who know not the Lord. And while they are taught to fear Him, they never turn to Him, but do as they like, worshipping their gods. Burning incense in the high places, serving idols and passing their children through the fire as sacrifices.

When God sends lions in the land to provoke them, the king of Assyria sent a priest of Israel among them, to teach them of the God of the land, but they still made gods of their own.

If there will be a stubborn and wicked people, bowing and serving false gods in the land, better they not be carrying the name of Israel, better to not be claiming to be His people. A lesson modern Israel should heed.

teachings.title: The light promised to David is Christ
teachings.summary: Judah was spared only for the promise to David, whose light is Christ, and the failed first covenant shows the Jews have no promises apart from Christ, against Dispensationalism.
teachings.text:
Next we are given news of the kinds of Judah, and their slide into the same abominations as Israel, the ways of Ahab. And their falling away led to Edom and other nations revolting from being tributaries. Blessings given to David and Solomon now wasted.

*Yet the Lord would not destroy Judah for David his servant's sake, as he promised him to give him alway a light, and to his children.*

That promise is to David, and the light is Christ Jesus.

Dispensationalism makes the promise to the wicked Jews, and the light their own being. We can see plainly that the only thing keeping Judah from being utterly destroyed as Israel soon will be, is the promise to David for a King to rule forever in Jerusalem, the place where the Lord puts His name.

God had delivered on the covenant made in the wilderness to bring the children of Israel to the promised land. He kept His covenant that as long as they kept their end of the deal, and didn't turn to false gods and the abominable things the Canaanites did, He would be their God.

But that covenant was already failing by this time.

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

Just another example of the unbiblical nature of Dispensationalism and the idea that Jews remain God's chosen people, or that they have any promises other than Christ remaining.

teachings.title: God chose David and Jerusalem, not the Jews
teachings.summary: God preserved Judah for David's sake and for Jerusalem where Christ would die, not because the Jewish people were chosen, and their broken covenant was replaced by a new one, so reject dispensationalism.
teachings.text:
God says to Solomon; *Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father's sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son. Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake which I have chosen.*

As we see in this chapter, the Lord begins to put into motion various threats for the kingdom, and sends the prophet Ahijah to Jeroboam, to give to him the northern kingdom of Israel, divided from Judah. Saying;

 *I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand, and will give it unto thee, even ten tribes. And unto his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there. And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel.*

Notice that it is not the Judeans whom God is concerned with, or a covenant with the people. The Jews, as they will come to be called. The covenant the Lord made is with David, and His concern is with keeping Jerusalem because that is where God chose to place His name; Christ Jesus.

Dispensationalists falsely claim that it is the Jewish people who God chose. But it was always a winnowing, and of Judah He chose David. The city of Jerusalem was chosen before there even was a tribe of Judah. Before Abram was Abraham.

God had a purpose and a plan and it was that the Son be made flesh and dwell among us and be put to death in the same place Abraham willingly offered Isaac by faith.

**Genesis 22:7-8**
*And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering? And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.*

The seed of Abraham, that would bless the whole world, was Jesus. The son of David, the King that would rule forever, is Christ.

God preserved the one tribe not because of their own righteousness; *Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in mine eyes, and to keep my statutes and my judgments.*

They failed to hold up their end of the covenant made with their fathers in the wilderness, that had they kept the commandments of the Lord, they would be His people, and He would be their God.

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

Reject Dispensationalism

teachings.title: God is not bound to Israel after the flesh
teachings.summary: Israel was only ever spared for the sake of Christ the promised Seed, and like Israel bringing the ark to battle, dispensationalist Zionists wrongly trust in a covenant rather than in the Lord.
teachings.text:
This passage is particularly relevant in these days of wars and rumors of wars. God is not bound to always be with Israel after the flesh. Even at this time, in ancient Israel, God only protects them to maintain His seed, which is the birth of Christ.

**Isaiah 1:9**
*Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.*

**Romans 9:29**
*And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.*

The times that the Lord had saved Israel after the flesh, was solely due to Christ. His Seed. Nothing else made them any different from the other peoples of the earth.

And here we see them trusting not on the Lord, but on the covenant.

*So the people sent to Shiloh, that they might bring from thence the ark of the covenant of the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth between the cherubims*.

They were as dispensationalists are today, saying that because the covenant exists or existed, that's all they need. They didn't have to keep it themselves. And so their trust wasn't with the Lord, but on their own entitlement.

Whatever victories Israel had in the past was to the furtherance of delivering Jesus in Bethlehem, The Word made flesh. And whatever deliverance they had came from them calling upon the name of the Lord for salvation. Their salvation came by faith.

And when a wicked people who do not have Christ presume that by their own nature, God is obligated to defend them, He will not hear their cries.

There's so many lessons teaching against the heresy of dispensationalist Zionism. And they were written for our admonition here in these last days.

teachings.title: Promises to Lot and Esau, and nations judged
teachings.summary: God gave land to Lot and Esau too, yet destroyed those nations for wickedness, so modern Jews have no claim, for God gives and takes away the bounds of nations.
teachings.text:
Here in **Deuteronomy 2**, Moses continues his retelling of the time in the wilderness, the 40 years recounted in part in the **Book of Numbers**. There are some perspective changes and details added that broaden the underlying history, and containing details that flesh out the story.

A few things that stand out to me in this reading; the promises of land to Lot and Edom, and the nature of the giants that were in many of these lands.

Modern "Jews" and their Zionist pets will make quite a big deal about the conditional covenant made in the wilderness to deliver the land to Israel, which had been promised to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ. A promise repeated to Issac and Jacob. They claim ownership as the nation of Israel (by deception, but none the less) based off this idea that they are the inheritors. But the promises to Lot and Esau were to the nations they spawned, by the blessings of God, and yet those nations were destroyed in time, and the land taken as spoil, after the wickedness of the people. The same as Israel. The same as the remnant in Judah. God judges nations on this earth and their bounds and habitations are His to give and take away.

teachings.title: Broken off for unbelief, grafted in by faith
teachings.summary: The unbelieving Jews are cast off and blinded, and are grafted in again only if they believe, while Gentiles who grow highminded can be cut off just the same.
teachings.text:
*For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?*

This is the entire point of Paul's arguments about the Jews. They are cast off. They are blinded. They are reprobate, just as Jeremiah preached against Israel;

*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

But wouldn't it be wonderful if the veil were lifted that they may come to believe on Christ?

Now the dispensationalist will say that in the end, on the day of redemption, they will look up and see Jesus coming in the clouds and believe and be saved. But that is taught nowhere in scripture.

Paul gives us the actual means by which *some may be saved*. Provoked to jealousy. Provoked to emulation. By what? The mercy and grace shown believers by God. By His glory revealed in the believing Gentiles. The people who were not a people.

This theme runs throughout the epistle. There is no glory but God's. And this is how it is revealed. Mercy and wrath.

It is not up to us to ask why some are fitted to mercy and others to wrath.

This isn't God picking and choosing, but providing the means of salvation, and foreknowledge of who would avail themselves, all elect in Christ Jesus. All who are predestinated by faith in Him to be conformed to Him and His likeness. All who believe become elect and because God predestinated all who believe to be elect and adoption and promises and blessings and to be the seed of Abraham, the father of faith, whether Jew or Gentile. It's the process that was put in place, by the lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

And so knowing this, and having shown the Gentiles of the sorry state of the fallen Jews, Paul warns against thinking Gentiles are some kind of special boys, falling victim to their own conceits the way the Jews have.

*Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.*

If generations of Christians began taking for granted the grace given to them, and assuming it is because they are better than the unregenerate Jews in terms of their own righteousness, they too could be cut off. Blinded just the same.

Some take Paul's caution to the Gentiles to mean something entirely different, that the Jews are saved by some other means. But we have systematically proved by going through Romans that that isn't the case.

Some will say the holy root are the Jews, and that while some branches are cut off and others grafted in, they still are the chosen of God by genetics.

But the true vine is Jesus. It is entirely by grace. There is no difference.

*If they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again.*

Simple as.

All this is to encourage mercy for their enemies for the Gospels sake, that Christians can maybe convert some by believing on Christ. That some of the Judaizers might get saved.

*For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.*

Israel was to be a light unto the unbelieving world. Now the believing world is to be a light to unbelieving Jews. All to God's glory.

*O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out! For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor?*
*Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen.*

teachings.title: Dispensationalism falls apart by comparing scripture
teachings.summary: Dispensationalism survives only on proof texts stripped of context, and falls apart when scripture is compared with scripture.
teachings.text:
Anyone who tries to justify Dispensationalism to defend their Zionist fever dreams and heretical end times doctrine has to rely on making each argument in a vacuum. Stripping proof texts from their surrounding meaning. By ignoring contradictions and clear verses, to make doctrine from non sequiturs.

But when we compare scripture to scripture, their doctrines fall apart.

That is why they will make sweeping proclamations and assertions and arguments that are only backed by the stripped-away proof text, and not by the whole context of Scripture.

It is why their false teachers will discourage reading the Bible yourself. Studying to be approved before God. They will over complicate it, make you doubt the word. Use false translations, study guides and charts. Tell you you have to "God back to the Greek!" or Hebrew. Imply that if you don't understand it the way they present it, you must not be saved.

And inevitably, they will use Judaizing to bring a false gospel of works to reinforce their own wicked doctrines.

Dispensationalism has crept in to good, KJV, Bible believing churches with the right Gospel, no doubt. And many saved Christians are misled by it.

But if you look at how far along the spectrum of Dispensationalism they are, the more damnable heresy creeps in.

A little leaven leavens the whole lump.

teachings.title: Joint heirs with Christ, not with Jews
teachings.summary: Believers are adopted sons and joint heirs with Christ, while unbelieving Jews in the flesh cannot please God and have no claim to the promise.
teachings.text:
Paul is transitioning from the previous arguments, to build upon them that salvation is by faith. By the Spirit and not the words or by the deeds of the flesh. But again, in contrasting the law of the flesh with the law of faith, Paul shows how the promises and inheritance are to those that believe. That believers are adopted sons of God, crying Abba, Father. That the Spirit itself bears witness to this adoption. That we are the children of God, and those without Christ are none of His.

We are heirs of God, joint-heirs with Christ. Not co-religionists with Jews. Not co-heirs with them. But with Christ. And unbelieving Jews have no claim to the promise.

Unbelieving Jews living by the law of the flesh die after the flesh. It is only by the Spirit of Christ that the deeds of the body are mortified, made dead. To no effect. Because we live, made alive by the Spirit.

But Jews are dead in their flesh. Not of His. Not children of God having not the Spirit of adoption. Not heirs of God or co-heirs with Christ, because they reject Him. They are carnal. They have the spirit of bondage. They are of the flesh.

*So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.*

Similar to **Hebrews 11:6**;
*But without faith it is impossible to please him...*

The unregenerate Jews are of the flesh and have not faith. They cannot please God. The Bible says it is impossible. The wrath abides on them to the uttermost.

But the dispensationalist will say they will come to believe. They will come to faith in the end. "God isn't through with His people."

And yet the same dispensationalism they profess claims they will be reinstituting the works of the law. The sacrifices and the ordinances, which we know is the ministration of death. It is the law of the flesh, and by this law it is impossible to please God.

The contradiction of their heresy cannot stand up to the scrutiny of the word. *Let God be true and every man a liar.*

teachings.title: Abraham justified by faith, not circumcision
teachings.summary: Abraham was counted righteous by faith before circumcision, so the promise comes by faith and fleshly Jews have no claim on the Abrahamic covenant apart from Christ.
teachings.text:
Building upon the conclusions reached in Chapter 3, we see in **Romans 4**, Paul uses scripture to flesh out the ideas and demonstrate the truth of his argument. The veil lifted, so that by the reading of Moses a believer may understand God's word.

He begins with the understanding that Abraham was not justified by his works or by circumcision, but by his faith. Abraham believed God and it was counted for righteousness.

And when Abraham believed, it was decades before the institution of the carnal ordinance of circumcision. A practice giving an outward sign for the continuation of the people chosen to bear Abraham's seed, which is Christ.
