While **Romans 4** is frequently cited to demolish the heretical argument that we are saved in any capacity by our own works, it is primarily an argument against the Judaizers who think to themselves to say they have Abraham as their father.

But as John the Baptist says in **Matthew 3:9**;

*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It wasn't circumcision that saved Abraham, but faith. It wasn't even his willingness to sacrifice Isaac. All the great works of faith by Abraham may be reason to glory among men, but not before God. They may be reckoned for reward out of debt, but not of grace which is freely given to those who believe, to the glory of God.

As David wrote, Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Those who do no works, but have believed on Christ, that faith is counted for righteousness.

It is an accounting. The only thing that is reckoned for forgiveness of sin and salvation from death, is faith.

And so, if this blessing came by faith and not circumcision, there is no profit in circumcision.

And if the righteousness of Abraham came by faith, there is no profit in being able to call Abraham your father after the flesh.

The promise of God, that through his seed all nations shall be blessed, and that seed should be made heir to the whole world, was not made to Abraham, or to his seed through the law. Meaning his physical descendants, who under the law are inheritors.

The promise to be made heir was through the righteousness of faith.

This excludes unconditionally any claim Jews would have on the Abrahamic covenant, except by faith in Christ.

*For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect*

If dispensationalist Zionism were true, that by the law Jews are heirs to Abraham's promise, *then faith is made void and the promises made of none effect.*

Saved Christians who believe that Jews are the inheritors by this promise, are like Esau, selling the promise for pottage. Despising their inheritance.

teachings.title: Dispensationalism in light of Romans
teachings.summary: Romans 1 lays the foundation against reading Romans 11:26 as Zionism: the gospel of Christ was promised by all the prophets and the dispensation of grace has been in effect from the beginning.
teachings.text:
**Dispensationalism in light of the Book of Romans.**

The events of the past week have seen an increase in the false claim that modern Jews occupying the Levant are the Israel of God, not saved believers. To defend this heretical garbage, those supporting this claim will use a handful of scripture, but they especially rely on **Romans 11:26**;

*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob*

Stripped of context, this appears to support their false teaching, but luckily for us, we have the entirety of Romans to demonstrate why this interpretation is wrong, and frankly dishonest.

For the next few days I am going to go over the building blocks for the arguments made by Paul in Romans to refute that reading of 11:26, once and for all. Starting today in **Romans 1**;

*Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God, (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,) Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ*

In **Romans**, the often abused epistle to the believers in Rome, Paul makes several arguments, and in the Spirit, these arguments build upon each other, each underpinning the next.

Here in the opening greeting, Paul stipulated several important and fundamental points as a foundation of everything that follows.

Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ, separated unto the Gospel of God. This is important. It isn't separation from; it isn't separation from the world, from sin, from his previous beliefs prior to salvation. It is towards something, with a purpose. And that something is not only the Gospel of Jesus in the sense we generally think of, the 4 books that tells us His life, teachings, death and resurrection, but Paul places the entire canon of scripture up to that point, the Old Testament as we refer to it, as the good news of God, because to Him all prophets gave witness.

As Christ says;

**John 5:46-47**
*For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?*

This is important to establish. Jesus being the fulfilment of the prophets and the oracles of God sets the context for everything that follows. Paul is going to give the final word on the Dispensation of Grace, and how it relates to both Jew and Gentiles. And this dispensation has been in effect from the beginning. It is of God, given in sundry times and diverse places to the fathers by the prophets, moved by the Spirit.

The only new revelation is that it is Jesus who is called upon, the mystery of salvation that always existed, revealed in these last times, that all who call upon the name of the Lord are saved.

The promise of God in Christ, His good news that He's been telling the patriarchs and the Hebrews in general, from the beginning, that Jews always had access to. They *should* know and have recognized who Jesus was.

Paul then gives a concise rendition of that Gospel by which he and the Romans he is writing to (and we today), know we are saved:

-Jesus was **made flesh** through the seed of David
-Declared **the Son of God** with power. Many signs miracles and wonders. Raising the dead and healing the sick. Preaching the word with authority, etc, **According to the Spirit of Holiness**
-And **by the resurrection from the dead**
-**By whom we received grace**, apostleship, **called of Jesus Christ**.

God became flesh and dwelt among us, was killed and raised from the dead as God promised, and all who answered the call are given the grace of God, the gift of eternal life. Called to follow Him and spread this good news to all nations.

teachings.title: The Jews have no role in end times prophecy
teachings.summary: Jews have no role in the end times except destruction; the third temple is Christ and His body, and any rebuilt temple or sacrifices would be an abomination.
teachings.text:
One of the most helpful things in understanding end times Bible prophecy that I can recommend is forgetting everything you've ever heard about the Jews and their role in it. And then let the Bible speak.

Jews hold no role in in the end times aside from being utterly destroyed and cast into the lake of fire. They may help set up the antichrist and be betrayed so that the days of vengeance can occur. But other than that, they are meant to be a synagogue of Satan who will be made to see that God loved us who believe.

God isn't waiting on them to build a third temple. The third temple is Christ and the body of believers. Anything they build will not be called the Temple of God. It'll be an abomination.

God isn't waiting for them to return to doing sacrifices, and if they do, it too is an abomination. Blaspheming Jesus who is the only sacrifice.

teachings.title: The alms for Jerusalem were for believing saints
teachings.summary: The collection for the poor saints at Jerusalem was temporary relief for believing brethren in a famine, not a mandate for Christians to fund unbelieving Jews forever.
teachings.text:
As Paul begins to wrap up the letter with his intentions to visit the churches in Rome, which he will eventually if not in the manner he thinks as he wrote this, he delves into some of the plans he has made that will delay his journey.

One of those things is the bringing of alms to the church at Jerusalem, collected from the churches throughout Asia Minor and Greece to benefit the believers there suffering through a great famine, as we were shown in **Acts 11**:

*And in these days came prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch. And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judaea*.

This is discussed in other epistles, and is very specific to the time and place and need. It is about saved brethren in the Jerusalem of that time, in the famine that plagued the land as it drew nearer and nearer to its destruction. Relief from the other churches of believers, that the brethren of saved believing Jews and others in that church may ride out the hardship to the glory of God.

Many enemies of the Gospel take the following verses from **Romans 15** and twist them into something else;

*But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints. For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem. It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.*

Unbelieving Jews twist this to guilt Christians into supporting all Jews. All the time. Begging for money in the most obscene ways, and tricking those weak in the faith into thinking they are mandated to fund "Israel" forever.

But we have been made partakers of their spiritual things only in Christ. The need was temporary. For believers. Brethren caught in the midst of God's wrath upon the rest of the Jews.

Others cite this passage in the same manner as the unrepentant Jews, claiming we are cucked by our faith, and required to serve Jews. This isn't the case and it is always interesting to me how much in common Jews and pagan Gentiles have in regards to their abuse of scripture to tell us what we believe.

teachings.title: Let their eyes be darkened
teachings.summary: The prophets and Jesus cursed unbelieving Israel, and bless them that bless thee is fulfilled in Christ, not in anyone calling himself a Jew.
teachings.text:
As David wrote, cursing Israel in **Psalm 69**; *Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.*

(Note all the cursing of Israel in the prophets and Jesus' preaching. They were not afraid of being cursed for it. The "bless them that bless thee, curse them that curse thee" being fulfilled in Jesus, not anyone calling themselves Jew)

Paul hopes that, as God said repeatedly in the OT through the prophets, He will provoke them to jealousy by the salvation of the Gentiles. By giving the Kingdom to another people, they will repent.

Paul says that if God is glorified in the salvation of the Gentiles by the destruction of the Jews, imagine how much more glory God would have if the Jews as a nation, would repent and believe?

teachings.title: There is no respect of persons with God
teachings.summary: Jew and Gentile face the same judgment and revelation, refuting the dispensational idea that Jews are favoured by God.
teachings.text:
Again this argument Paul is making is to provoke the Jews to jealousy and into separation towards the Gospel, and to reject being holier than thou against the repentant pagans being converted in Rome. But this entire exchange is also important to understand when dealing with Zionism and the Dispensationalist error that Jews are favored by God.

There is no respect of persons to God.

The Jew and Gentile are judged the same. Given the same revelation of wrath. Have the law in their hearts, given a conscience, the Spirit working to convict them of sin. All to bring them to the knowledge of the truth, that salvation comes by Christ and the Gospel. By the spirit of the law, not the letter.

All face the same judgment. None have an excuse. And our following the letter of the law doesn't make us better than those who aren't where we are spiritually. Only the grace of God is keeping us from the same fate.

This doesn't mean we don't judge, it means we should try to judge righteously as God has with us.

And never think you are a special boy, given favor by God for who you are, what tribe you're born to, how diligently you keep the letter of the law, but remaining humble in the grace of God.

teachings.title: God is able of these stones to raise children
teachings.summary: John the Baptist rebuked the Jews for trusting their lineage from Abraham, repudiating the special treatment for the Jews that dispensationalists still teach.
teachings.text:
Here in Luke chapter 3, we find his goal, stated in the opening of his Gospel to "*set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us*," being met, giving precise details to the time in which John the Baptist, followed by Jesus, began their ministry. Luke establishes who was in charge, and where, pinpointing for readers the time and place of this happening, with familiar figures of their recent past; *That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.*

And so we find John, born roughly 6 months ahead of Jesus, has fulfilled the prophecy given his father by Gabriel, to be the answer to the prophecy given Isaiah; the voice in the wilderness making straight the paths of the Lord.

In the times before modernity, when the lords and kings would travel abroad, often in caravans, taking weeks or months to get where they were going, a group of their servants would run ahead, both to herald their lord's passing to prepare those in the path chosen to receive their king, and to make certain the road was clear. That the way was smooth. Harbingers and workmen.

So too, Christ the Lord was coming and the paths were to be made straight for Him.

In scripture, we often see the idea of walking in God's statutes, following His wisdom, being righteous by obeying His sayings, is compared to walking a path. Turning neither to the left not right. But following the narrow way of the Lord.

John, the harbinger of the Lord is sent by God to spiritually make straight the paths, to bring the people to repentance, turning towards His Son. Baptizing those who believed, a picture of Christ's crucifixion, burial and resurrection, and a symbol of their being washed clean by the remission of sins. Preparing them that shall see the salvation of God among them. Exhorting those who were saved to now do the works meet for repentance. Charity. Proper living. Changed as those who are free from the wrath should live.

John is filled with the Holy Ghost, as promised, and speaks boldly and with authority the words of God. He is the first prophet of the Lord to have the Holy Ghost upon him in 400 years. His hard preaching against sin and of the word of God, scripture, draws people from all over the region.

We see the lands mentioned by ruler, and it encompasses all of Judea, up into Samaria and the provinces from the sea and in and around Jordan, and it is from these places that multitudes come to hear John preach and to be baptized.

In **Matthew 3** we see that this draws attention of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and that the preaching he does, also shown in **Luke 3**, is an indictment of the Jews, especially their religious leaders.

*O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

John speaking in the Spirit says that if they are truly there repentant of their false ways, show the fruit of it. Especially the religious leaders who have not the fruits, the souls prepared to repent towards God. They've failed the people. They have rested on the fact that they are God's "chosen." They haven't prepared anyone for the salvation to come.

This generation of vipers has believed that by the nature of their lineage they would be saved. This is the same mistaken idea behind dispensationalism and the "God's not done with the Jews!" mentality among so many misguided and judaized Christians today.

But John repudiates the idea of special treatment for the Jews. He says God could raise up Israelites from rocks if He so chose. They aren't special boys. And they certainly aren't living in a manner that shows God-fearing reverence for Him and His laws.

teachings.title: I Regarded Them Not
teachings.summary: Hebrews 8:9 shows the Jews broke the covenant and God regarded them not, so salvation was never by bloodline but always by faith.
teachings.text:
The entire New Testament is a case against dispensationalism and the idea that Jews are still "chosen," and exempt from the faith of Christ unto forgiveness that is the New Testament, the *better* covenant. But Hebrews 8:9 is one of many silver bullets, putting down the heretical idea that Jews today are special:

*Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

God's covenants, His promises to a nation, like all covenants, carry if-then statements that if not fulfilled, exempt the parties from its terms. The Lord says here in no uncertain terms that the Jews continued not in His covenant AND I REGARDED THEM NOT.

It can't be any plainer. Just as John the Baptist says to the Pharisees, *Think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It was never about genetics or bloodlines, except so far as the promise of Christ, which wasn't to the Jews but to all men. The root and the seed.

And salvation from Hell and death was always by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord. But the law that served to convict those who transgressed, a schoolmaster, is replaced by the law in man's heart, and the knowledge of the truth in Christ Jesus.

The Old Testament then, which some still believed they were under as Paul wrote this, was ready to vanish away.

teachings.title: The Woman Is Not Modern Israel
teachings.summary: Scofield's teaching that the woman is Israel twists Joseph's dream to prop up a pre-trib rapture and Jewish kingdom, while Revelation mentions Jews only as persecutors.
teachings.text:
Just to reiterate, the Scofield view that the woman is Israel, in order to maintain the Dispensationalist view of end times Bible prophecy, is wrong. Nothing about it fits other than the 12 stars of the crown, the moon and sun, and even that is a stretch.

They use as proof text the story of Joseph and his dreams from **Genesis 37**:

*And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me. And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth? And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.*

This dream puts Joseph as the focus of the worship by his brothers and parents. His father, a man, was Israel. Not a woman. The stars were not a crown. The sun and moon may have been Jacob and Rachel, but again, the presence of a sun and moon as clothing on the woman doesn't work, as Jesus human lineage is through Leah to Judah.

This interpretation doesn't make any sense. But they need it to be modern Israel in order to make the prophecy that follows of a pre-trib rapture and Jewish earthly kingdom, fit. Like most all of their Zionist heresy, they have to take liberties with literal scripture and lean on interpretation of symbolic verses to make it all work. And they will say in no uncertain terms that their interpretation of this chapter and who the woman is as the only correct one.

*Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night. And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death...And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.*

Modern Israel and the Jews who are only mentioned in Revelation in a negative light, as persecuting the saints in a like manner with Satan's war upon believers and are called a Synagogue of Satan. That's it. Every other prophecy and promise is to believers, of every kindred and tongue.

The worship of Jews and their god, Satan, is the entire point of dispensationalism and Scofield's twisted interpretation of the Bible.

teachings.title: No Promise of a Third Temple
teachings.summary: Scripture promises no third temple after 70 AD; Scofield invented this teaching, and any sacrifices offered by Christ-rejecting Jews would be an abomination.
teachings.text:
Reaching the midpoint of Revelation, we see John receives a rod made of a reed to measure the temple of God, but not the outer court. This is tied in to the 3rd Temple prophecy, commonly used by the Dispensationalists to say it must be rebuilt at some point before the Great Tribulation begins.

A proof text offered for the building of the 3rd Temple comes from **Haggai 2:7-9**: *And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the Lord of hosts. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the Lord of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the Lord of hosts*.

Other than this, there is no scripture that promises any new temple will be built in Jerusalem after God used Rome to destroy it in 70AD. Scofield, that viper, is one of the primary sources of this understanding, and his study notes have deceived millions over the past century. Jews in the Tanya, a book of the Chabad Lubavitch Zionist Jews, also claims that Jews will rule the world when the temple is rebuilt and their Moshiach comes.

It's possible. There's obviously attempts to get the Temple Mount cleared of the mosque that currently occupies it. There are fund raising efforts by evangelicals and hyperdispensationalist false prophets, saying they are going to rebuild.

The argument that some form of a temple must be built comes from **Daniel 9:27** regarding the antichrist and the takeover of Jerusalem:

*And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate*.

Basically, the antichrist and the Jews are allies for a year, before he turns on them and will cause offerings of sacrifices to stop, and raise the abomination of desolation in their midst. The argument is, no temple, how could there be sacrifices?

We will see in the second half of Revelation that there will be a New Jerusalem, adorned like a bride and given to Jesus as in a wedding. The old Jerusalem is not really important. As John writes a few verses later, Jerusalem is spiritually called *Sodom and Egypt*, *where also our Lord was crucified.*

God's not a fan.

It is entirely possible the destruction in 70AD and the ceasing of sacrifices and oblations is part of a dual fulfilment. It's difficult to say. We can just go by what is in God's word, and it isn't entirely clear.

One thing that is for certain, if the dispies are correct and the Jews manage to build a 3rd temple and begin making sacrifices there, it will not be pleasing to the Lord. They won't be to Him, as they have not the Son, neither the Father. The sacrifice was always a picture of Christ. If they worship there, it will be itself an abomination and the animals sacrificed to Satan.

teachings.title: The Synagogue of Satan Persecuted Smyrna
teachings.summary: Christ calls those who say they are Jews and are not the synagogue of Satan, which Zionist and dispensational churches fail to see.
teachings.text:
*And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive;*

Again, addressing the church of Smyrna, as the *first and the last, which was dead and is alive*. This is Jesus. Alpha and Omega. The risen Christ.

*I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.*

The church at Smyrna is poor, but rich in spirit. They are working for Christ and being persecuted for it by the Jews, so-called. The synagogue of Satan.

The absolute failure of those churches that teach Zionism and dispensationalism, Hebrew roots and other Judaizing heresies to recognize precisely who Jesus is talking about here - **HINT: they call themselves Jews and meet in synagogues** - that failing is the work of Satan in them. They are enemies of God, contrary to all men, and they kill and persecute the saints, liars and antichrists.

The tribulation they gave the early churches has never stopped.

Here, Christ encourages them that despite the tribulation of being jailed, it will be for ten days, and even if they die for His name they will be rewarded with crowns in heaven for their patience and eternal life for their faith.

*He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death*.

Another promise to the saved; we shall not be hurt of the second death, which we will see later in Revelation refers to Hell and the lake of fire. The eternal damnation that those who have not overcome will suffer.

teachings.title: Covenants have conditions: the fall of Edom
teachings.summary: God gave Edom a promised land then destroyed it for its iniquities, showing covenants have conditions, against the Zionist claim that God's land promise is unconditional.
teachings.text:
One thing to note regarding God's destruction of Edom, this follows hundreds of years of blessing them with the land of Seir which was promised unto Esau. But their betrayals against Israel, worship of false gods, taking advantage to raid Jerusalem with the Babylonians, it was enough and God took their land and made it desolate.

So many dispensationalists rest their Zionism on "God keeps His promises!" with no recognition or understanding that covenants have conditions. That God judges nations on earth. Here we have an example of a promised land, kept by God, given warning by God through David, and ultimately destroyed for their iniquities.

teachings.title: Not replacement but rejection
teachings.summary: Like Esau the Jews despised their birthright by rejecting Christ and became spiritual Edom, which is rejection, not replacement, the younger receiving the blessing by faith.
teachings.text:
Now, the Bible says that God hated Esau, and Jacob He loved. This is referring to the nations that come from each, Jacob giving birth to the 12 patriarchs of Israel, Esau the nations of Edomites. Much is made of this distinction, but the fate of Edom is not necessarily reflected in the life of its patriarch, Esau. In the next chapter we will look more closely at that.

For now, the parallels to Cain and Abel, Sarah and Hagar, Isaac and Ismael, Jews and Gentiles, even Jesus and Barabbas, the free will choices given to show that God favors faith over the law, spirit over the flesh, blesses them that trust His promises and do His will, giving them the inheritance for their faith, and the casting out of those who are after the flesh, even if by law they have a birthright claim.

The entire Old Testament serves as a pattern for the salvation to come offered in Christ. Both the choice to believe, placing faith above flesh, explaining the theology of the New Testament with examples from the Old. And continually we see the eldest by law passed over, to serve the younger, who by faith receives both the birthright and blessing.

When applied to the Jews and Gentiles, this is called "replacement theology," which is a misnomer. Like Esau, Jews sought an earthly kingdom from an earthly messiah, to satisfy their fleshly desires. They sold their birthright, despising their inheritance, by choosing to kill Christ. By rejecting the blessing that had carried them from Canaan to Egypt, back to the promised land. Through wars, invasions and captivity, they lost everything, for the younger, the Gentiles, to gain.

It's not replacement, it's rejection. Spiritual Edom. And like Edom after the flesh, they were made desolate by the Lord.

**Jeremiah 49**

*10 But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is spoiled, and his brethren, and his neighbours, and he is not.*

*11 Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me.*

*12 For thus saith the Lord; Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken; and art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink of it.*

*13 For I have sworn by myself, saith the Lord, that Bozrah shall become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all the cities thereof shall be perpetual wastes.*

*14 I have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent unto the heathen, saying, Gather ye together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle.*

*15 For, lo, I will make thee small among the heathen, and despised among men.*

*16 Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the Lord.*

*17 Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.*

*18 As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the Lord, no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.*

teachings.title: Dispensationalists selling the birthright to spiritual Edom
teachings.summary: God did not replace Edom; the Christ-rejecting Jews are spiritual Edom, and dispensationalists who honour them sell their own birthright for man's approval.
teachings.text:
God didn't "replace" Esau with Jacob. Edom with Israel. The choice is made in man's heart.

And the Jews who killed Jesus and the prophets and persecuted the Gentiles who received the inheritance in faith, are spiritually Edom. The wrath of God abides upon them to the uttermost. They are a byword and a parable. A warning.

Modern, dispensationalist Christians who have elevated Jews to coequal status, even giving them honor as "older brothers," claiming that inheritance of the flesh, in the law means they retain the birthright and blessing they rejected when they reject Christ, are carnal and risk going the way of Edom themselves.

They so despise their birthright in Christ they are willing to give it up to Jews for a morsel. For less than a bowl of pottage.

They say the "church age" ends in failure. Taken up in a pre-trib rapture to make way for the Jews to receive the Kingdom that is ours in Jesus' name. They question the judgment of God and ignore these warnings found throughout the Bible, in exchange for...what? The false teachers get paid. Hagee and the televangelists and evangelical pastors who promote dispensationalism get filthy lucre, for sure. Vipers being rewarded in the flesh. But the flock, many who are believers, they get nothing of value but the brief and fleeting feeling of approval by a group of people who resent and hate them. "If I bless them I will be blessed!" If you are saved in Christ you've already been blessed! If you live in the spirit, doing the will of the Father, the blessings are ours, in abundance.

But for the meaningless approval of man, they sell it all to the wicked, spiritual Edomites.

And like Esau, they will see eventually that their choice robbed them of the blessings, and with tears they will repent, but it will be too late.

teachings.title: God's promises to Abram, not the modern state
teachings.summary: God's promise to bless them that bless Abram was personal to him, not to the modern Jewish state, and Abram was saved by calling on the Lord.
teachings.text:
All of Genesis, as important as the stories of Adam, Cain, Noah, the flood and Babel are, was prologue to this. The story of Abram and Sarai. Abraham and Sarah.

Up to this point, mankind who called upon the name of the Lord had the promise of His blessing and protection, of God being their savior, but not the specific promise of the man Christ Jesus. Born of man. Seed of Abraham. Here we see that the LORD appears unto Abram and makes him promises.

- I will make of thee a great nation
 - I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing
- I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee:
- and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

These are direct blessings and promises to Abram, himself. Many try to take the personal promise to Abraham, to bless those that bless him and curse those that curse him, and claim it's an eternal promise to the modern Jew and the apostate state calling itself Israel. This is found no where in Scripture. This is God's promise to protect him and his wife, as God has called Abraham to go to a different land, to Canaan, and there He would establish his legacy.

*And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and the souls that they had gotten in Haran; and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan.*

There, God appeared again to him, and gave this more specific promise; *Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the Lord, who appeared unto him.* *And Abram called upon the name of the Lord.*

He was saved by faith through grace. Note the timing of when that was. It comes up later in scripture.

This promise was made to a 75yr old, childless Abram in a place where *the Canaanite was then in the land.* His altar built between the Mediterranean and Jordan, between Galilee and Jerusalem.

The LORD appearing to Abraham is considered by many to be an Old Testament appearance of Jesus. A theophany. As the Bible says at no time has man seen the Father, many consider the appearance of God unto man in the OT a representation of Christ, who was from the beginning with God and is God.

Next we are given a familiar story of a famine in the land, of going to Egypt to sojourn. Of Pharaoh and plagues. This theme of finding refuge and sojourning in Egypt is a picture of young Jesus being taken there by Joseph, just as Jesus' stepfather's namesake will.

There in Egypt, worried that Sarai, his 65yo wife, who was still apparently very fair to look upon, would be taken from him, and that he would be killed, Abram tells her to lie and say they are siblings.

This seems to be a lack of faith by Abram, and causes enmity with Pharaoh, who indeed was going to seek to betroth Sarai, but now, subject to plagues by the LORD, angrily asks them to leave the shelter of his kingdom.

God cursed those who would curse Abram, despite his lapse of faith. God made that promise to him, and if he trusted God, he wouldn't fear for his life. As it stood, God came through anyway, but Abram and all his household were sent away back to Canaan and the famine.

teachings.title: No chosen people but in Christ
teachings.summary: Paul refutes the idea that Jews are God's chosen and Gentile believers lesser, there is only the one dispensation of grace, and Rome's sin of presumption keeps people from assurance.
teachings.text:
Again the focus of these first 3 chapters is attacking the idea that Jews are God's "chosen people," and that Gentile believers are somehow less-than in their inheritance. Paul puts this false notion to bed, emphatically. We are the second born who received the full inheritance and blessing. The Jews having sold it in their fornication for the pottage of earthly things.

Dispensationalists rely on the appearance of the word 'dispensation' in these passages, to justify their wicked heresy, while the text of it destroys them. There is only the dispensation of grace. The change is to extend it to all men, through Jesus Christ regardless of lineage.

There is no limit to the atonement, but the free will to believe the Gospel by those that receive it, and *In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.*

This destroys the damnable "mortal sin of presumption" made by the Catholic Church to snare the unsuspecting into never coming to salvation, and never having that confidence, put in bondage to dead works of the law, and reliant on the RCC to save them in the end. Sending millions to Hell.

teachings.title: Jacob have I loved: the table made a snare
teachings.summary: Malachi shows the Jews already despising God's table 400 years before Christ, so God turned His name to the Gentiles because the fault was theirs.
teachings.text:
Malachi, the last prophet before John the Baptist, likely preached to the restored Jerusalem sometime during the absence of Nehemiah, when the leader returned to Persia, as we saw in the last chapters of his book. When the people immediately turned again to sin and iniquity.

The theme of the Lord turning from the people whom He loved, and provoking jealousy by prophesying that the heathen would come to Him is clear and unmistakable.

The burden of the Lord comes upon the prophet, and he preaches the word, that the people, especially the priests, have turned from Him, saying He doesn't love them, and they curse the table of offerings He instituted.

He says Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated, pointing to the destruction of Edom while Jerusalem stands restored. He says that the nation of Edom, from the same seed of Abraham through Isaac, brother to Jacob, is cursed to show them His love. That the Lord be magnified in Israel. And yet, they do not honor Him as sons should a Father, or as servants a Master. They despise His holy name.

They offer corrupt sacrifices. Polluted bread upon the altar. They say the table of the Lord is contemptible.

**Romans 11:9-10**
*And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.*

God is cursing them as David cursed the people.

God asks, if they brought the sacrifices of the lame, the blind, the polluted to their Persian appointed Governor, would he be pleased with it? How should He, being the Lord of hosts?

Malachi says, I pray you beseech God that He will be gracious unto us. Because God no longer is respecting them as persons. He regards them no more. Their altar and offerings He rejects.

And so, He says that His name, the name of Christ Jesus, shall be great among the Gentiles. A pure offering.

*But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the Lord is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible.*

They were already rejecting Christ. 400 years before His coming. This is important to understand, that it was finding fault with THEM that another covenant, a better testament, offered to the nations of the world, in the blood of Christ.

He curses them, and the deceiver, both the priests that gives a corrupt sacrifice while saving the pure, male ram, unspotted, for himself. And their father, Satan. The deceiver whose deeds they do.

Because the Lord's name is dreadful among the heathen. Dreadful meaning inspiring fear and awe. And they would accept Him the Jews rejected.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Jerusalem as dross
teachings.summary: Jerusalem broke the old covenant through idolatry, false prophets and oppressing the poor, despised God's longsuffering, and was judged and cast out like dross, which is why a new covenant was needed.
teachings.text:
We see here in the preaching against Jerusalem, where the Lord demands the prophet tell the Jews of their abominations and His judgment, that much of it mirrors those things given to Moses in the wilderness. The things God proclaimed should be dealt with by death. That the blood be upon the wicked and not on the people in the land.

But the children of Israel failed to uphold their end of the covenant and now faced the promised judgment.

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I Made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The longsuffering of God, that nearly 1,000 years passed from Sinai and the law to the utter destruction of Jerusalem, was taken by the people to mean God wasn't present. That He no longer cared. That maybe He wasn't real.

His mercy and calls to repentance, ignored. The grace He offers men because of His love, taken advantage of. For greed and lust.

And false prophets preaching lies, saying "The Lord has spoken," when He hadn't. And devouring widow's houses and taking advantage of the poor and the fatherless.

**Matthew 23:13-15**
*But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves*.

The Lord looked for the righteous to be the salt that preserves, and found none. Just like in Sodom, where He told Moses if there were found just 10 righteous men, He would spare the cities. And so He promises to gather the wicked and melt them in flame like the molten metals they make their abominations with. For sacrifice in the mountains. For their idolatry, for their shedding of blood. For their degeneracy. Extortion, usury, greed.

They have become as dross. Impurities in the silver, cast out.

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

teachings.title: God's writ of divorce to Jerusalem
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 16 is God's divorce of unfaithful Judah, worse than Sodom, judged by her spiritual state rather than lineage, with hope only in Christ.
teachings.text:
In **Ezekiel 16**, Jerusalem is personified as a woman whom God rescued, adorned, and entered into a covenant with (verses 6–14), akin to a marriage.

However, her persistent idolatry and unfaithfulness (v15–34) provoke God’s judgment, described in terms of punishment and abandonment (v 35–43). The chapter reads as a writ of divorce. God breaking up with her, in a spiritual metaphor.

When God found her, she (Judah specifically here, but Israel generally), they were as the Canaanites. Worse, they were abandoned. Alone. Again this isn't literal and genetic, but their spiritual condition. Abram was a Chaldean. Jacob was a Hebrew, as Abraham lived in Hebron.

There was intermarriage with the Canaanites, but the analogy is not about lineage but beliefs and idolatry.

When God lays out their abominations, giving the fine clothing, incense and worship to strange gods that was meant for Him, and murdered the children He gave them it is adultery and worse than the abominations of Samaria (Israel) or even Sodom.

The idea that what they did was worse than Sodom and her daughters, the like cities around them, is a theme. The worst place imaginable, and yet unfaithful Judah is worse:

**Isaiah 1:9**
*Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.*

**Matthew 11:24**
*But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.*

They despised their oath. They broke the covenant. They behaved like their sisters, humanity that didn't know better or didn't have the privilege that He had bestowed upon them. The line of David. The glory of Solomon. The oracles of God, the Temple, the blessing and the promise. And so God is righteous to divorce them.

But, despite this condemnation, the Lord leaves room for hope. Christ is coming. And not only would Judah be restored, but her "sisters," the Gentiles. That He will establish His covenant, and we shall know He is the Lord.

teachings.title: The Lord rejected all the seed of Israel
teachings.summary: God rejected all the seed of Israel, keeping the Jews only until the promise of Christ came, after which unbelieving Jews were destroyed and God regarded them no more.
teachings.text:
As for the Southern Kingdom of Judah, God had made a promise to David for an eternal King from his lineage, and a promise to put His name upon Jerusalem. But the Jews themselves?

*Also Judah kept not the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they made. And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his sight.*

The Lord rejected ALL the seed of Israel. So, while Judah had protection for a while longer, and was then carried away to captivity in Babylon for 70 years, and though they were returned when some had turned back to the Lord, were allowed to rebuild the temple and dwell in the land, they were never again given the blessings that came as a nation to the children of Israel. We will see as we go through scripture, that they were under Babylon, Persia and the Medes, the Greeks, and by the time of Christ, under the Roman empire.

The Jews, the remnant of Judah and Benjamin and Levi that returned to Judea after being freed from 70 years captivity, were only kept from utter destruction until the promise of Christ came.

And once Jesus ascension was done, and the gospel went out to all the world, the temple was destroyed and the remnant of unbelieving Jews were put to the sword, scattered and destroyed.

God regarded them no more.

teachings.title: Forty years from the cross to 70 AD
teachings.summary: The generation that died in the wilderness pictures the unbelieving Jews cut off, forty years from the crucifixion to Jerusalem's fall in 70 AD.
teachings.text:
*I will smite them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of thee a greater nation and mightier than they.*
...
*How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me. Say unto them, As truly as I live, saith the Lord, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward which have murmured against me. Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun. But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised. But as for you, your carcases, they shall fall in this wilderness.*

This story is also a picture of the casting out of the unbelieving Jews in Christ's time and the early church. Of their being cut off and denied the Kingdom.

Dispensationalists cannot see that the so-called Jews are like this generation, that despised the land promised to them. And only a believing remnant, like Caleb and Joshua, would be allowed to enter therein.

*After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years, and ye shall know my breach of promise.*

Jesus was crucified in 30AD by the reckoning of the Passover and 3 sabbaths in a row before His resurrection. 40yrs later was 70AD and the Romans destroying Jerusalem, the Temple and killing and scattering the remaining Jews.

The passing of a generation, left to die in the wilderness, never to enter into the Kingdom, the promised land. The breach of God's promise made known to that wicked and gainsaying generation.

Amen

teachings.title: His blood be on us: the Jews crucified Christ
teachings.summary: The Gospels show the Jews, not the Romans, demanded Christ's death, and Jesus prophesied judgment on them as the old covenant was done away at the cross.
teachings.text:
And so we see the multitudes of the Jews come up from the High Priest's home, to be accused before Pilate that the Romans may kill Jesus for them.

Pilate examines Jesus and says to the chief priests and to the people, I find no fault in this man. Jesus is the lamb without blemish.

And hearing that Jesus is of Galilee, not of Judea, and having Herod who is protectorate of that region in Jerusalem for the feasts, sends Jesus unto him. Herod too finds no fault with Christ Jesus, but his men shamefully mock Him, dressing this "King of the Jews" in purple, as the Jews slander and bear false witness that Jesus may be slain. Returning to Pilate, he calls the Jews accusing Jesus to him, saying, *Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him.* And was to give Jesus stripes as chastisement, but the Roman governor was to set Jesus free.

But the Jews insisted, "Crucify Him!"

This Biblical truth is considered "antisemitic blood libel" today, in many supposed Christian churches. You will see this today, as various priests and pastors will make public statement and social media posts blaming the Romans for the death of Christ.

But the Gospels tell the truth. In **John 18**:

*Then said Pilate unto them, Take ye him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death.*

In Matthew 27:

*Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.*

**John 19**
*But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar.*

And as Jesus says to the mournful women of Jerusalem, here in **Luke 23**, as He carries His cross, beaten bloody, face unrecognizable, stripes on His back bleeding so much they pressed Simon of Cyrene to help bring the cross up the hill; Jesus says:
*Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us. For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?*

Remember, that the spring feasts and holy days, the first of which being Passover and the feast of unleavened bread, represents Jesus Christ and His first coming. The time of green wood, newly budded. The fall feasts, with the trumpets and harvest, the time of dry trees, which are kindled for fire. Here we see Jesus' prophecy against the Jews in the end times, even as He is led to His death by them.

It is undeniable that the people who were chosen by God to be His ministers of the Gospel to all the world, who had a covenant to be His people, a holy nation, an example and light unto the world bringing repentance and salvation, utterly rejected their inheritance, and so, with their killing Jesus the veil in the temple was torn in two. The Old Testament done away with. Its ordinances nailed to the cross with Christ.

teachings.title: Your house is left unto you desolate
teachings.summary: Jesus' lament over Jerusalem which killed the prophets marks His being through with those reprobates, who would not see Him until the day of wrath.
teachings.text:
*The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.*

The spiteful Jews of Galilee threatening that Herod was looking to kill Jesus, that they would get Him to leave. He laughingly says tell that old fox that He still doing work and will abide a while. He's got devils to cast out and people to heal, that He'd be finished in three days. Showing no fear, because Jesus knows where and when His death should come.

And, because Jerusalem is where the Jews always killed the prophets, He says to the Pharisees *it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.* It is a slam against them, and must have pricked their hearts with shame and anger.

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.*

He is through with these reprobates. He is done, saying you won't see Me until the day of the Lord. The time of wrath. When every knee shall bow. He tried to get them to believe but they would not. And now, they are done. Twice-dead. Cut off. His destiny drawing near, but theirs is present before them. Weeping and gnashing of teeth, cast out into outer darkness in the lake of fire.

teachings.title: The Days of Vengeance on Judea
teachings.summary: In Luke 21 Jesus speaks of the Jews as they and them in the days of vengeance, matching the Gentiles treading Jerusalem in Revelation 11.
teachings.text:
**Luke 21**

2*0 And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.*

*21 Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.*

*22 For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

*23 But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.*

*24 And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.*

The Olivet discourse in Luke, which Jesus gives us details of the end times contains this passage regarding the days of vengeance, where those who are within Judea are destroyed. Now. Of course, dual fulfillment aside, this fits in with Revelation 11 and the Gentiles trampling the holy city underfoot.

It's interesting that Jesus refers to these people, they, and them. Talking of the Jews as another, whereas believers He will say thee, ye and thou.

But here Jesus describes the invasion and destruction of the Jews which corresponds with the beast and his armies eliminating them in the end times during the wrath period of the second three and a half years.

teachings.title: The cursed fig tree withered from the roots
teachings.summary: The fruitless fig tree pictures Judah, cut off forever for bearing no fruit, which is not replacement theology and refutes the dispensational claim that God is not done with the Jews.
teachings.text:
The chapter opens with Mark's telling of what is popularly known as Palm Sunday, though it occurred on a Saturday. The Jerusalem crowd hailing Jesus, riding on the colt of an ass as in prophecy, as he arrives for the Passover, of which He will be the sacrifice.

The colt is there where He said, and they allow the disciples to take it, as He said. Because everything in this world is God's and His to use for His glory.

Then we have a telling of the fruitless fig tree. Jesus, seeking fruit finds none and curses the tree that it will produce no fruit forever after, and the tree is withered and destroyed from its root.

*No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever... And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots. And Peter calling to remembrance saith unto him, Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away.*

It is not "replacement theology," it is the taking away of the Kingdom for failing to provide fruit, not bringing souls meet for repentance unto salvation. For rejecting the stone, cut without hands, laid as the cornerstone before the foundation of the world.

For the "God's not done with the Jews!" false doctrine, this story is twisted, because a plain reading is perfectly understandable. We see more in **Matthew 23;**

*And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.*

This is a literal story that holds obvious symbolism regarding the Jews, here at the end of Christ's earthly ministry. Fruit, as always in the Gospel, means saved believers, those faithful to God and saved by His promise, in His Son, Jesus.

It's reminiscent of a parable in **Luke 13:6-9**;

*He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground? And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.*

The tree is Judah. The Lord, God the Father, the dresser, Jesus Christ. His earthly ministry, to the lost sheep of Israel was the final attempt to produce fruit of that tree. And having no more fruit, it was cut down and destroyed.

God's word is clear, it is forever that the tree is destroyed. It is cut down. It is cast into the fire. Never to bloom again.

The dispensationalist lies are built on denying scripture.

teachings.title: Romans on the Jew and the elect
teachings.summary: Quotes Romans 2, 5, 9, 10 and 11 and shows that Paul argues salvation is by faith, so Jews after the flesh are not the elect and dispensational promises to physical Israel do not follow.
teachings.text:
*Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God...Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God? For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.

For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.

What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God. For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid...

What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin; As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.

Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God. Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law. Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.

What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all

Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead; Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.*

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

9 Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.

There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit....So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.

For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

 I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost, That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen. Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.

What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?

As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved. And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God. Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved: For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth. And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha. What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone;*

*As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved. For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.

For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you. But Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me. But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.*

*I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work. What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.(According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.

And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway. I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid: but rather through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy. 

Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness? For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify mine office: If by any means I may provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them. For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?

For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again. For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree? For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in. And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the father's sakes. For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance. For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy.

For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all. O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!*

It's impossible to get any notion of dispensationalism or a promise to physical Israel being saved from this text. 

Paul creates an airtight argument that salvation is by faith, that the adoption and promises by faith are for the elect, and that Jews after the flesh are not the elect and have not obtained it.

teachings.title: The remnant of Israel and the false gospel of Zionists
teachings.summary: Uses 1 Kings 19:18 to show that in Old Testament days only a remnant of Israel was saved by grace through faith, answering the claim that all of fleshly Israel will be saved in Romans 11.
teachings.text:
**1 Kings 19:18**
*Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him.*

The dispensationalist Zionists who claim to be Christian but offer a false gospel for Jews, and another for Gentiles, Make it out as if when Paul writes, *all of Israel shall be saved* that he's talking about Israel of the flesh. 

But as we see under the Old Testament, There were periods where of the millions of Israelites, there were as few as 7,000 people who had called upon the name of the Lord for salvation and were saved by grace through faith. 

The strait is the gate in narrow the way and few there are the find it.

teachings.title: Romans 9:22-24, vessels of wrath and mercy
teachings.summary: Reads Romans 9:22-24 as one question about God's longsuffering with the vessels fitted to wrath so that the riches of His glory are known on the vessels of mercy. Says not all are Israel that are of Israel, and that God always intended to offer salvation to the whole world.
teachings.text:
**Romans 9:22-24 **

*What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: and that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?*

All one question. What if the vessels fitted unto wrath, (Gentiles), He endured with longsuffering that He might make known the riches of His glory on the vessels of mercy, even us (Jews)? 

They are not all Israel that are of Israel. 

God in His providence always intended to offer salvation to the whole world.

teachings.title: One way of salvation in every dispensation
teachings.summary: Says animal sacrifice was never a means of salvation and that dispensationalism errs in claiming a different means of salvation for ethnic Jews in the end times.
teachings.text:
I don't know who needs to hear this but animal sacrifice never was a dispensation or ministration of salvation or grace or a means of justification. The blood of bulls and goats could never take away sin. 

There's only ever been one ministration given to save souls, and that's calling upon the name of the Lord and trusting in Him alone. We have a dispensation to administer the gospel to all men.

The biggest issue with "dispensationalism" isn't the past, it's the unbiblical claim that there will be a different means of salvation or a different dispensation in the end times, reserved for ethnic Jews.

teachings.title: Scripture on the conditional old covenant with Israel
teachings.summary: Lists passages that show the old covenant with the physical nation of Israel was conditional and done away.
teachings.text:

teachings.title: Thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter
teachings.summary: Zechariah 11 prophesies judgment on Judah's false shepherds and the breaking of the covenant, and his price of thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter is fulfilled in Judas' betrayal of the Good Shepherd.
teachings.text:
Continuing in Zechariah, we see the prophet turn from active encouragement in previous chapters to a more negative message and future prophecy against Judah.

The doors of Lebanon, the cedars, the oaks of Bashan, which is the fertile eastern bank of the Jordan, these represent the built temple, the great city Jerusalem, forged by the timber from these areas. Zechariah is prophesying their destruction, when reconstruction has hardly even begun.

The leaders, the shepherds, howl at their loss, the young lions roar, because the pride of Jordan is spoiled by false teachers and bad leadership at the judgment of God against them.

These wicked leaders, God says, slay the people and hold themselves not guilty. They sell them into servitude and think they are bless by the riches that comes to them for the price of men. The shepherds have no pity for their flock.

And God says this is His judgement on the Jews. Sort of the flip side of **Jeremiah 3:15**

*And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding*.

So, Zechariah preaches the destruction of the people at the hands of their neighbors and the kings and the Lord will not deliver them as He has so many times. As He just had from captivity. This is a future event.

God will feed the flock to the slaughter.

This all could be a prophecy of 70AD and the destruction of Jerusalem. The temple, as Christ said would come. Not on stone standing upon another. The scattering and spoil of the pride of the Jordan. The burning of the cedars and oaks. Or dual fulfilment with the days of vengeance, the end times prophecy of the destruction of Israel.

**Luke 21:21-22**
*Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

The prophet takes up two shepherd staves, and on one staff he writes "Beauty" and the other is called "Bands."

He says three shepherds he cut off in one month, and that he hated them and they hated him. False teachers, it seems. I can't say if this is Zechariah rebuking them, and taking their followers away from them, or God speaking directly that He did this to them. Either way, the flock of Judah is then cut off.

He breaks the staff "Beauty," which is the covenant with the people. Note the poor of the flock who believed on Him knew this was the word of the Lord. As a prophecy of Christ, and the new covenant that was established, the poor knew Jesus was the Word of the Lord.

Then he asks the people for his price as shepherd, and they set it at 30 pieces of silver. The parallel is obvious.

**Matthew 26:14-15**
*Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver*.
