The good Shepherd, valued at only a lowly sum, 30 pieces of silver to be betrayed. And says to cast the sum to the potter.

**Matthew 27:3-7**
*Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in.*

The act of throwing the money to the potter was a symbolic rejection in Zechariah, and the purchase of the potter's field with the money is the fulfilment.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple: a promise on condition
teachings.summary: The temple vision was a conditional promise to Israel of Christ and a kingdom if they repented, which they refused, as Christ lamented over Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
Ezekiel is no different. It is the explicit purpose of the Temple prophecy, giving the people a promise, contingent on their getting right:

**Ezekiel 43:10-11** 
*Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, shew them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the goings out thereof, and the comings in thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof: and write it in their sight, that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them*.

The promises given the people included Christ, and a Kingdom, if they repented towards the Law and God.

**Zachariah 6:12-15**
*Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is* The Branch*; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord: Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of the Lord. And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the Lord, and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto you. And this shall come to pass, if ye will diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God.*

They could be children of the Kingdom if they were ashamed of their abominations, took the chastening God consistently gave them, and like the heathen of Nineveh, turned from the wicked ways,

God sent prophets, and they killed them. God wiped out the Northern Kingdom as an example. He brings Judah into bondage under Babylon, and makes His holy city desolate. All to goad them to come to repentance that they would be His people, and He would be their God.

**Matthew 23:37**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

teachings.title: Jesus is the promised Shepherd
teachings.summary: When Jesus says I am the Good Shepherd He declares He is the Lord of Ezekiel 34, whose flock is believers, not Jews after the flesh.
teachings.text:
Jesus is the promised Shepherd.

He maketh us lie down in green pastures. He searches out for the lost. He heals us he feeds us and watches over us from our enemies.

He judges the other cattle for their treatment of his sheep and the pasture that he had given them and the waters he had provided them.

Notice here in Ezekiel 34, which begins the hopeful prophecies of Salvation in the last part of the book, that the Lord says *Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out*.

He uses this assurance a few times. When Jesus says *I am the Good Shepherd*, He is directly stating that he is the Lord.

Further down, we see *even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* Just as Jesus is the Son of God, He is a son of David.

And there are sheep of other folds that he brings in and makes us one fold. This is the promise. It is not to Jews after the flesh. It is not to a physical nation of Israel. Although certainly the fold has sheep from among them.

But the bad shepherds are the religious leaders, false prophets and wayward priests of Israel. And further the Lord says he will judge His flock, and cattle with cattle, these are the physical Jews, after the flesh. He's clearly delineating between believers and unbelievers. Between His sheep who hear His voice and those that trample down the fields and pollute the waters.

The promise of eternal peace, safety and security, freedom from attack of enemies without and corruption from within, is all given to His flock.

*The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.* Amen

teachings.title: Statutes that were not good
teachings.summary: In Ezekiel 20 God gave idolatrous Israel and Judah over to strong delusion and statutes that were not good, as Romans 1 describes, while still pleading with their hardened hearts and promising the kingdom to come.
teachings.text:
This cycle continued, and in Judah as well. *Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live*.

He gave them over to strong delusion, that they may believe a lie. He allowed them to see what happens when they trusted their own foolish hearts that were darkened.

**Romans 1:21-25**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

They went to the high places, Bamah in Hebrew, instead of the mount of the Lord, the Temple of Zion in Jerusalem. They worshiped idols in His name and offered sacrifice to them, and ultimately passed their own sons through the fire to Baal. Even those that sat down to enquire of the Lord this day.

*Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers? and commit ye whoredom after their abominations?*

God pleads with them as He did with their fathers, that His word against them would prick them in their hardened hearts. That they turn from the sins of their father to embrace the truth of the Lord God.

To that end, He says He will put them to the rod. And destruction and desolation. That He will purge the unrighteous from among them. But if they repented not, so be it. The Lord asks one thing of them, stop doing their gifts and offerings and abominations to their idols in HIS holy name.

*For in mine holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord God, there shall all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offerings, and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all your holy things.*

This isn't only the restoration of Jerusalem after the captivity. But a prophecy of what would come.

This is the Kingdom of Heaven. This is the holy reign of Christ. This is the final assembly of believers, who will be sanctified before the heathen for His holy name, Jesus. And we shall know that He is the Lord.

teachings.title: Hephzibah and Beulah, the bride
teachings.summary: The bride married to the Lord is the New Jerusalem, and Judah was spared only for David's promise and the place of His name, never for the Jews themselves.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 62** is a love letter from the Lord for the city of Jerusalem, the mountains of Zion, the land where God chooses to place His holy name.

The valleys and the mountains made straight, and level for the King's Highway. The path of the King.

*Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah* (the delight of), *and thy land Beulah* (the bride*): for the Lord delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.*

This again calls forward to the events described in **Revelation 21**, which I posted yesterday. The New Jerusalem that depends from Heaven, decked as a bride.

People often talk about the wedding of the church to Christ. I know it's used as parable a couple times, but the actual feast is here and the bride that golden city, where Christ will reign forever.

We've seen it again and again in the Chronicles and Kings, and from the prophets, that the only reason Judah wasn't destroyed like Sodom, like Israel, was the promise to David, that the Christ promised to Abraham would come from the King's lineage. And, every time, to keep Jerusalem as the place God chose to place His name. As the spot where Jesus would be offered. And where He would triumphantly reign.

It was never the Jews. They were beneficiaries of God's plan. They were not His plan, themselves.

And when the city was made desolate by the captivity, the exile to Babylon. And, in the Great Tribulation, when the abomination of desolation is made, when many would say that Jerusalem is "Forsaken," that it will not be. That Christ's redeemed will flock to Jerusalem, a crown of glory. A royal diadem. The symbol of His power.

teachings.title: The election of grace
teachings.summary: Argues from Romans 11:5-6 and Galatians 3 that election is of grace, and that salvation for the Jews as Abraham's seed makes grace no more grace.
teachings.text:
Every damnable heresy in "professing Christianity" is based on rejecting the election of grace. They make grace contingent on merit, making grace no more grace. 

**Romans 11:5-6**
*Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

Grace is the undeserved and unmerited favor of God. 

Here in Romans, Paul is writing to explain why physical Israel, Jews after the flesh, are not elect. That their blood relation to Abraham cannot save them. That it is by the election of grace man is saved. Continuing in verse 7;

*What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.*

Which election? The election of Grace. And so, the heresy of dispensationalism fails when the scriptures are searched to see if it is so. And the damnable heresy of hyperdispensationalism is undone by the doctrine of grace. 

**Galatians 3:16**, **26-29**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ*.

*For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.* *For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The Jews being saved for being the seed of Abraham makes grace no more grace.

**Romans 9:6-8**
*Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.*

teachings.title: I am the LORD, there is none else
teachings.summary: God's specific prophecy of Cyrus proves He alone is God and that His promise of salvation in Christ is just as sure, and the Israel that shall be saved is all who are Abraham's seed by faith in Christ.
teachings.text:
Continuing the very clear, undeniable, easy to understand prophecy of God through Isaiah, of the future King of the Medo-Persian empire, more than a century off in the future. **Isaiah 45** is one of the most powerful chapters in the Bible.

God says He has named Cyrus as deliverer, for after the Babylonian captivity, still decades away, after the 70 years of desolation in Jerusalem as prophesied, the Babylonian empire will be over thrown, and Cyrus will free the Jews wot return, to rebuild the temple. That the line of David continued to Christ and the place God put His name would stand until it served its purpose, the death burial and resurrection of Jesus.

And just as sure and specific and certain as this prophecy is for Cyrus, so it is for the Messiah.

By this we may know there is no other God beside Him. He is the Lord, and there is none else.

For all creation testifies, and all the prophets gave witness, and all the promises made to the faithful, and the evidence all around that those who trust in Him are never ashamed.

God calls all His shots beforehand, and we see the results are true. And if these things are sure and true, then know the promise of salvation and eternal life in Christ Jesus is as well.

*Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together; I the Lord have created it.*

The Lord has created all things that, in His time, in the end, salvation and righteousness are as a flood upon the earth. And like the flood of Noah, we shall be delivered and those that reject God will be destroyed.

Those that chase after gods of their own hands, who worship the created more than the Creator, shall be confounded and ashamed when the day comes.

*But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.*

The Lord openly declares these things, all that is right. His perfect law. His kept promises. His holy Name.

*I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.*

**John 5:37**
*And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.*

**Philippians 2:9-11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father*

**1 John 5:7**
*For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.*

The word of God is true, let every man be a liar who rejects it. All that are incensed against Him shall be ashamed. Those who do not wish to retain God in their knowledge, who hold the truth in unrighteousness, they will be made to know He loves us.

And in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and glory.

**Galatians 3:27-29**
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

**Romans 11:26-27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Amen

teachings.title: The breaker is come up: God visits evil on evil
teachings.summary: Micah's gathered remnant is the Israel of God by faith, and we can take comfort that bad things happen because men choose evil, and God repays evil upon the wicked.
teachings.text:
Finally, Micah again prophesying about Christ:

*I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men. The breaker is come up before them: they have broken up, and have passed through the gate, and are gone out by it: and their king shall pass before them, and the Lord on the head of them.*

This promise is to we who are saved, who are the Israel of God and seed of Abraham by faith as much as it applies to believers in the Old Testament.

We should take comfort that the enemies of the Lord, haters of truth, the violent and degenerate, the thieves and the liars, all will face God's wrath. That they chose evil and rejected the opportunity to be saved. That God will repay.

Why do bad things happen? Men decide to do them. Why does God "allow" it to happen? He doesn't, but instead visits evil upon evil. We can rejoice knowing the wicked will have their day of judgement, even as we praise Him for our salvation with fear and trembling.

teachings.title: Israel a reprobate nation
teachings.summary: From Hosea 4 he teaches that Israel, not wishing to retain God in its knowledge, was given over as a reprobate nation to be consumed by its sins, the same judgment coming on the world.
teachings.text:
Continuing the preaching against Israel, its people are wicked, especially even their priests, those low men that were established by Jeroboam, when he introduced idolatry to the people and caused all Israel to sin.

Hosea preaches hard against their sins; the violence and bloodshed, the drunkenness, the literal whoredoms and adultery, and spiritual; chasing after false gods.

The Lord says that if they don't wish to retain Him in their knowledge, they will perish for that lack of knowledge. If the priests won't reprove and rebuke sin, then they are in common cause with it. Let their sins consume them. God won't even scourge them for backsliding. They've been given up and given over, a reprobate nation.

They go to the stocks for advice, that is to wooden idols, sacrifices in groves, seeking favor of their dead gods. So the living God says let their daughters and wives go whoring as they have to Him.

What a wicked time, and the destruction of Israel was long past due. Only the longsuffering love of the Lord stayed their end.

The Lord does make provision to keep the evil out of Judah, that the false religion and fornications of the North, the Idolatry of Ephraim, would not spread into the Southern Kingdom, for now.

What a condemnation. And it is the same righteous judgement of God that will be passed on to the world, even as Judah, or that is saved Christians today, are spared. It may seem like the wicked prosper and go unpunished, but as we see here, that is a punishment in itself. Allowing the blood to heap against them, their own sins to make them miserable, even as they compound. And then, destruction.

Perfect is the judgment of God

teachings.title: Hosea buys back the adulteress
teachings.summary: Hosea's redeeming an adulteress pictures God expecting faithfulness from Israel through desolation, because in the latter days they would seek the Lord and David their king, who is Christ.
teachings.text:
Here again, the Lord instructed the prophet to play the cuckold, to love a woman as a friend who is an adulteress, just as Israel played the harlot to their God.

The Lord is that man, the people wickedly left His protection and provision for wine and idols, as an unfaithful wife.

Hosea purchases the service of a whore for a pittance, (15 pieces of silver is half the 30 that is the price of a servant, a measure and a half of barley, barely enough for bread), but with the expectation of faithfulness, to represent the desolation that is to come upon Israel and Judah. A time where the plenty of God is taken away. No king, no sacrifice, no priestly duties, no image to bow to. And yet He wants them to know by this preaching that the Lord expects them to suffer through this loss and still maintain their faithfulness to Him. Something they weren't able to do in plenty, now do in tribulation.

But why? Because of the promise of the Lord, that in the latter end of things, they will seek the Lord their God and David their king, being Christ Jesus, and receive His goodness once again.

teachings.title: The covenant with David kept in Christ
teachings.summary: God's covenant of an everlasting throne was made to David, not to the Jews or any modern state, and is kept in Christ, yet its blessings are conditional and the saved are chastened when they sin.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **1 Kings**, and the reign of Solomon, we see that after 20 years, and much building and growth of his wealth and power, Solomon has completed the temple, and his palace and fortified Jerusalem and built up cities throughout Israel. He has been blessed by God, given tribute by many, gifts such as the city given by Pharaoh to his daughter, Solomon's queen. And through extensive trade and the loans and goodwill of the Phoenician King, Hiram (Huram in Chronicles), Solomon has made Israel a great nation.

But first he began with the Lord.

And so, 20 years after the first visitation of the Lord, God again appears unto Solomon, pleased with his faith and devotion. And He reiterated the covenant made with David, and to say Jerusalem is the place He has put His name, forever. That God's heart and eyes shall be upon it in perpetuity. The Lord says;

*And if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded thee, and wilt keep my statutes and my judgments: Then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom upon Israel for ever, as I promised to David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man upon the throne of Israel.*

This covenant, that there shall be a king forever over Israel from David's lineage, is fulfilled in Christ Jesus. This is a personal covenant, not made to Jews or to the nation of the 12 tribes, or any modern state, but to David, and confirmed to Solomon, and kept in Jesus.

But the conditions of keeping the blessings that had so enriched Solomon and blessed the Temple he had built for the Lord, which He had hallowed for His name, were clear. That He would cut off the people if they or their children strayed, and the Temple cast out from His sight. Becoming a byword and an astonishment.

While Jesus rules over all things, forever the King of Salem, the blessings of that promise aren't without condition. We who are saved and become co-heirs with Jesus Christ, have the same understanding. That we, in this life are blessed by that promised King, and given eternal life and made sons of God, but we do not have a license to sin and disobedience is met with punishment and chastisements from our Father. Many a great Christian has fallen to this, backslidden and ruined in this life. Lacking proper fear of the Lord.

*Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought forth their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have taken hold upon other gods, and have worshipped them, and served them: therefore hath the Lord brought upon them all this evil.*

Never forget the Lord that led you from spiritual Egypt. From the bondage of the law, to make you His people. To whom much is given, much is expected.

teachings.title: The mystery: Gentiles fellow heirs
teachings.summary: He teaches the mystery revealed to Paul is that Gentiles are fellow heirs of the same body by the same gospel, preached to Abraham from the beginning.
teachings.text:
**Galatians 3** plays a foundational role in this hyperdispensationalist "Grace movement," as it's the main source for their teaching that Paul had a new mystery revealed unto him by Jesus, and it was a different gospel for the Gentile. But that's not what this says at all, in fact, as God often does in His word, He presents the idea of an unknown, a mystery, a dark saying, and then provides the answer key to understanding it. God is not the author of confusion.

Here, in verse 6, we have the answer to the mystery Paul is talking about; that the Gentiles should be fellow heirs with the believing Jews. Partakers of the Fathers promise in Christ, by the Gospel. Partakers and heirs OF THE SAME BODY. By the same Gospel. And that Gospel is identical to the one given by Jesus in **John 3:16**. Salvation by grace through faith. Eternal life for all who believe on His name.

Further Paul expounds that this mystery, of Christ going to the Gentiles that all nations be blessed, was always the plan, from the foundation of the world, and as explained in **Galatians 3:8**;

*And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.*

**Genesis 22:18**
*and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.*

teachings.title: Choose life: against Calvinists and Zionists
teachings.summary: Against dispensationalists, Calvinists and Zionists he teaches that God makes salvation an individual choice of the heart, Jews included, not forced or by birth.
teachings.text:
For the Dispensationalists, the Lord who cannot lie and Who keeps His promises forever, as they are fond to remind us, had this to say;

*But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it.*

"Aha, but if they turn again to the Lord they shall be graft in!" Yes. Individual jews who choose life, seek the Lord and find Him in Christ will be forgiven and be made heirs to the promise.

But that choice is theirs to make, as individuals, choosing between death and life in Christ Jesus.

Calvinists and Zionists share the same twisted theology; that God will force individuals to believe, just as He keeps them from obedience to the Gospel. But here in **Deuteronomy 30** (and throughout scripture) God makes it clear that we all have a choice. That it isn't by who we are, but what our heart believes. That it is by choosing to love the Lord, and in doing so, living by faith.

Choose life.

teachings.title: Clean and unclean meats done away in Christ
teachings.summary: He teaches the dietary laws were carnal ordinances picturing separation from the Gentiles until the reformation in Christ, and the peculiar people now are those cleansed by His blood.
teachings.text:
*These are the statutes and judgments, which ye shall observe to do in the land, which the Lord God of thy fathers giveth thee to possess it, all the days that ye live upon the earth.*

**Deuteronomy 14** continues the retelling of the law, originally given in the wilderness but now updated slightly for the settling of the promised land.

Here in chapter 14, following a warning against participating in scaring and ritual shavings that the heathens practiced in Canaan before them, mourning rituals that saw them shave their heads in unsightly ways, the Lord gives dietary laws against eating "unclean" beasts. Ordinances that had applied only to the Levites in the desert, but now apply to the Hebrew people as a whole.

*For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.*

Carnal ordinances given as a picture of the time to come, the reformation in Christ;

**Hebrews 9:9-10**
*Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;*
*Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.*

Dietary laws regarding clean and unclean were a sign given to show the separation from the Gentiles, a difference done away with in the New Testament. As the Lord showed Peter in **Acts 10:13-15**;

*And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat. But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean. And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.*

Here, not only lifting the ordinances but encouraging Peter and the other Apostles to give the gospel to the Gentiles. That the holy people were of the Spirit of faith. The peculiar people who God cleansed with the blood of the lamb, echoing Deuteronomy here in this epistle;

**1 Peter 2:9**
*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light*

teachings.title: God is a God of separation
teachings.summary: From creation onward God separates and divides to make a holy people, separating believing Israel after the Spirit from unbelieving Israel after the flesh, wheat from chaff, until the harvest is complete.
teachings.text:
Here we go.

God is a God of separation. The Bible has example after example of division, separating one thing from another. Day from night. The creatures after their own kind. Woman from man. Man from the Garden. Cain and Abel. The descendents of Seth, the sons of God that called upon the name of the Lord and the children of men who did not. Noah and his perfect generations from fallen man. The animals of the ark. The nations of Noah's sons. The people of Babel and their languages. The habitations of the nations. Abraham out of Ur. Ishmael and Isaac. Jacob and Esau. Joseph and his brothers. Hebrews out of their land and into Egypt. Out of Egypt and back in the land. The covenant with Moses that they would be a holy people. Separated from other nations.

Even here, in Numbers, each tribe separated and counted. And the Levites separated even further.

**Luke 12:51**
*Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:*

The division. The separation. Making holy a people of God. Separating Israel from Judah. And Jesus from the root of Jesse. Believing Israel from the non-believing Jews. The tares from the wheat. Sheep from goats. Israel after the flesh and Israel after the Spirit. Unfruitful branches cut off and cast into the fire. The election in Christ chosen to be graft in.

**Deuteronomy 7:6**
*For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.*

**Isaiah 62:12**
*And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken.*

**1 Peter 2:9**
*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light;*

Winnowing the chaff from the wheat. The earth is His threshing floor. The harvest is ongoing. We are in the last days, and have been since the first fruit of Christ, and the harvest of 5,000 made by the disciples on Pentecost. We shall bring in the sheaves for the Lord. To Him the increase. Until the fullness of the harvest comes in.

Amen

teachings.title: The law annulled as by a husband's death
teachings.summary: The law is the ministry of death made null by Christ's death as a marriage ends at a husband's death, so dispensationalists reviving it are like a widow taking her dead husband back.
teachings.text:
Addressing the Jew, brethren after the flesh, those knowing the law, Paul continues his argument that the law is the ministry of death, while the gospel of grace is unto life.

But to buttress the point, Paul uses the law to demonstrate how the law is made null by the death of Christ, just as a marriage is annulled by the death of the husband. The oldness of the letter is done away with for the newness of the Spirit.

Paul is again dismantling the idea of salvation by the law. The same law that Judaizers sought to bring to the new believers of the Gentiles. The same law that dispensationalists claim was the means of salvation for the Jews, and that it will be implemented again. As if a widow should take her dead husband again as a spouse.

 *O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.*

Amen 🙏🏻

teachings.title: The potter's power over nations
teachings.summary: The potter of Jeremiah 18 and Romans 9 is about nations, as God destroys some to show His wrath and His mercy on others, as with the Jews and Gentiles.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 18** begins a shift in the narrative structure, where for the past several chapters Jeremiah had made some effort to plead with God to not be too hard on Judah, and God explaining that they've condemned their own selves with their fornication, going after false gods. Not heeding the word of God from the prophets but following the vain jangling from the false prophets telling the people that they were fine and judgment wasn't coming. That they were at peace with God. Even as they burned incense to idols and baked cakes to the "queen of heaven."

But chapter 18 begins with God sending Jeremiah to observe a potter, who is spinning the wheel to turn clay into a vessel. And, seeing the potter discard a bowl that didn't turn out right, to make another that would.

While many take the potter analogy and make it about us as individuals, because God does shape us to be fitted for His purpose, the primary application here, and in **Romans 9**, is about nations, specifically the physical nation of Israel. The descendants of Abraham.

*O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the Lord. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel. At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it*.

As Paul writes, nearly 8 centuries later;

*Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour? What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory*.

We see that the context remains the same. The destruction of the Jews serves God's purpose, that His wrath be manifest, but also His glory in those raised up in His mercy, the Gentiles.

God's judgment against Egypt and Pharaoh allowed His mercy to be seen in the children of Israel. His destruction of the northern kingdom, as a warning to Judah in the south. Judah's destruction by the Babylonians that Jeremiah is preaching will allow God to be glorified in their eventual return. The final destruction of the Jews in their rejection of Christ opens the door to the Gentiles to be graft in.

God uses the judgment against nations to bring about the glory of His mercy to those that believe. His wrath revealed from heaven allows His mercy and grace to be manifest in those He will be saved in His son.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Judah rejected
teachings.summary: From Jeremiah 6 he teaches that Judah, with its false prophets crying peace, was rejected of God as reprobate silver, and that God judges nations the same way today, especially those called by His name.
teachings.text:
*For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace....Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

Jeremiah, in the Spirit, is preaching hard against Judah, which has become totally corrupt, and faces judgment from the North, by the invading armies of Babylon which God is warning He will allow to conquer and spoil them.

And the prophets and priests are telling the people "Peace. Peace" when there is no peace. They speak soothing words, withholding judgement, leaving the people with a false sense of security. That everything is fine.

That their sacrifices and their expensive, imported incense, the performative religious acts they do, will offset the Idolatry, fornication and wickedness.

Jeremiah preaches that this is not acceptable to the Lord and they will be spoiled and left desolate. Reprobate, rejected by God.

A millennium after God takes the children out of Israel, clearing the land of the nations that committed  abominations, driving then out before them, and here they sit facing the same judgment. The northern kingdom of 10 tribes, wiped out and dispersed by the Assyrians, and Judah about to be overrun by Babylonians. And despite the warnings of the prophet, none of them repent of their ways. They break the covenant and despite God's longsuffering, His wrath is upon them.

How can we not help but see the parallels and understand we face the same judgment?

God judges nations by their works, and especially by those who call themselves by His name. If those claiming Him, who say they are Israel, fall away, He is going to cut them off.

It is a real 🎯 you are here-moment.

teachings.title: The Scofield Bible's heresies
teachings.summary: The Scofield study Bible twisted scripture to teach Zionism, dispensationalism and the kingdom given to the Jews, and to accommodate false science.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 4**, a clear prophecy of the destruction of Jerusalem coming from Babylon, has the distinction of being the "proof text" for the first of many heresies found in the wicked Scofield study Bible.

Written at the turn of the 20th century, but with roots back to Darby, Scofield took scripture and turned it on its head to embrace Zionism, dispensationalism, teach the wicked doctrines of the "failure of Christ church," and the Kingdom being given to the Jews.

He also sought to take the then-current trends in popular science, falsely so-called, that had been developed by antichrists to shake faith in God and His creation, and square them with the Bible so that Christians would accept things like Darwinism and dinosaurs. Scofield first published in 1909, and just a decade later was the infamous Scopes Monkey trial, that saw Modernists clashing with Fundamentalists over evolution, among many other things.

teachings.title: Modern Jews as reprobate silver
teachings.summary: Modern Jews are not the descendants of the twelve tribes but a people defined by rejecting Jesus, given up and cursed by God as reprobate silver, which undoes the dispensationalist hope for their salvation.
teachings.text:
Before getting back into the chapter itself, I want to reiterate that whatever else they are, Modern Jews are not the sons of Judah from the Old Testament.

Whether they are Edomites or Khazarians, or some other people, regardless of what Kaiser Sose origin story and Jewish fables, We know they are not the descendants of the 12 tribes of Israel. To the extent they may have some of Abraham's blood in them, So does most of the world.

The one defining characteristic of all modern Jews, and by modern I mean going back to the first few centuries AD, or the foundation of Judaism 400 years after Christ, all Jews hold as their primary identity the rejection of Jesus. Be they Ashkenazi, Arabic, Turkish, Polish, Reformed, orthodox, atheist, conservative or liberal... Every single Jew is an antichrist. And God will make of them a synagogue of Satan.

Reprobate silver will men call them. For they have been given up and rejected by God.

I make this caveat because as we know, dispensationalism is about modern Jews, not the 12 tribes of Israel which no longer exist and haven't existed since 70 AD.

When they say that they think that God isn't finished with the Jews or that all the Jews will end up being saved at the second coming of Christ, they are talking about this reprobate group that the Bible says aren't actually Jews. They aren't even Israel after the flesh let alone spiritual Israel, which are all believers.

And God has cursed them.

teachings.title: No plan B for the cut off
teachings.summary: From Romans 11 he teaches that those who refuse to believe are cut off and made reprobate, and that doubting this by imagining a secret plan to win them back questions the judgment of God.
teachings.text:
And so, *As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the father's sakes.*

God would that they believe and be saved. He would glory in the older being brought back into the Kingdom with the younger. But it can only happen through faith, and those who refuse to believe are cut off and made reprobate.

*For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.*

It's all about faith. We are all in sin and grace is offered all of us.

*O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!*

Many find it unfair that some are cut off, they refuse to believe the Reprobate Doctrine, they doubt the judgment of God. They think He must have some secret plan to win them back. A plan B. But the only plan is Christ. And Him crucified. And it is not for us to question the judgment and mercy of God. He will have mercy on whom He has mercy. It's not up to us to tell Him, but to humbly submit to His will.

*For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor? Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen.*

teachings.title: They stumbled at that stumblingstone
teachings.summary: Gentiles attained righteousness by faith while Israel failed by seeking it through works, which is Paul's argument in Romans 9, not Calvinism.
teachings.text:
*What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?*

As the prophets spake, moved by the Spirit, God promised to bring men from all nations to be His. And as the prophets warned the Jews, that except for the seed, being Jesus, He would have destroyed Israel sooner, they would have been as Sodom. But being fitted to the purpose, He showed mercy, until establishing Jesus in Zion, a sure foundation for the believers, Jew and Gentile, but for the unbelieving Jews, a stumblingblock. A rock of offense.

And this is the argument Paul is making. It isn't about Calvinism or Jews after the flesh, it is about Christ. Whatever twisted doctrines can be wrung out of Romans 9, the context is clear:

*What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone*.

Gentiles, through Christ have found righteousness. Jews, through the law, death. Why? Because they sought their own righteousness through works, rather than seek the imputed righteousness of Jesus, by faith.

It is the same argument Paul has been making since chapter 1.

We are saved by faith. It is God's righteousness, not our own. It is for His glory, not ours. Boasting is excluded. We are but clay to be shaped. The Creator is greater than the creation.

teachings.title: Righteousness by faith, not circumcision
teachings.summary: Abraham was counted righteous by faith before circumcision, so no rite, baptism, or work is required for salvation, and the inheritance is by faith in Christ, not by fleshly descent as Zionism and dispensationalism claim.
teachings.text:
So this is the promise made by God that if we believe on the Son, we are saved by His grace. Our sins forgiven. No sin even being imputed upon us. Whether we work or not, because work is debt not grace.

Paul continues using Abraham's example;

*Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.*

Abraham did not receive the ordinance of circumcision until decades after his believing God's promise, and being saved by that faith. He was blessed with the accounting of righteousness when he did not know circumcision. So this promise, predating this rite of the Jews, means it does not only apply to the circumcised, but also to the uncircumcised. And so the promise of grace doesn't require circumcision, but faith alone.

This point is both specific to the issue of circumcision being introduced by the Judaizers in Paul's day, but also generally speaking, that there is no rite or ordinance that is required for salvation. Not baptism. Not any ritual or keeping of tradition. No works of the law.

*And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also*.

Abraham as the father of all who believe, the circumcision of the spirit, the generation of believers are partakers of the promise, that the righteousness of God is imputed upon us in faith.

*For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.*

The promise of God that Abraham believed was that through his faith, he would be made father to many nations, and inherit the kingdom of God. This promise was made possible in Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ*.

Unbelieving Jews felt they were owed the kingdom by God for being Abraham's seed under the law. That the inheritance was by blood, and the promise made to them after the flesh, and not in the spirit.

This is the basis for Zionism and the false doctrine of dispensationalism.

But the Bible teaches the exact opposite. There is no difference between Jew and Gentile. All are under sin. It is by faith only that we are made heirs. That the seed of the promise is Christ manifest in the flesh.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It is not an inheritance by the law but by faith. Like Esau and Jacob, the inheritance went to the younger. It was taken from the elder, who with tears sought repentance from God, but none was found.

**Luke 13:25-30**
*When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.*

teachings.title: Abraham the father of us all
teachings.summary: The law works wrath, so the promise comes by faith through grace, making Abraham the father of all who believe, and the Jew has no claim to him outside faith.
teachings.text:
*Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all, (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were.*

Because the law brings wrath, because we are all under sin, it isn't by the law we are saved. It is impossible for all have sinned.

As James writes in the parts of his epistles ignored-by-works salvationists;

*For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.*

Remember, there are none righteous. Knowledge of the law brings wrath. But faith, the grace of God.

We access His mercy and forgiveness through faith alone. Plus nothing, minus nothing.

And in grace we receive the promise given Abraham, and count as his seed in the spirit. Adopted into the kingdom of God. Made sons of God. Abraham is the father of us all who believe.

 *(As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were.*

God, who can see all things, the future which is not to us, and yet it appears as it were to God, who quickens the dead, who breathes life into our dead spirit, and who made this eternal promise to all who believe.

The Jew has no claim to Abraham, outside of faith. None. And to none of the promises made, for they all are fulfilled in Christ.

If it feels like I am beating a dead horse, understand that it is God's word that stresses this over and over again, because it is the Gospel, the good news, that is the entire point of scripture. To bring us into the promise through faith and the imputed righteousness of God.

teachings.title: Dispensationalism is wicked
teachings.summary: Christians fall for dispensationalism by trusting study Bible notes and videos instead of reading the word, which teaches the law could not save and there is no other gospel for one people.
teachings.text:
Saved Christians who fall for the lie of Dispensationalism do so because they don't read the word of God themselves. They are led astray by wolves in sheep's clothing. They are brought to heresy by study Bibles' footnotes and column notes, twisting scripture and hobbling the power of the word. By charts and YT videos, and appeals after the flesh, and false promises of blessings for blessing a people who reject God and His salvation in His Son.

How can the law serve as a schoolmaster if your teachers say it had the power to save? That God's covenants don't expire, while those it was with no longer consent to the terms? If there is another gospel for one people that doesn't apply to the rest?

It is wicked.

teachings.title: Pharaoh a picture of the reprobate
teachings.summary: Pharaoh's hardened heart pictures the reprobate and the Jews who deny Christ and forbid the gospel, who are given over to God's wrath to their destruction.
teachings.text:
The plagues against Egypt continue. We see Pharaoh's heart has been hardened. He cannot believe God's word, even to his own destruction and the destruction of his people.

And even as Moses is a picture of Christ, and the physical salvation of the Israelites from bonds in Egypt are a picture of spiritual salvation from sin and the bonds of the law, Pharaoh is a picture of a reprobate, and the Jews who deny Christ.

Just as Pharaoh refused to allow the children of Israel to go and worship God as He commanded, the Jews persecute Christians, forbidding the Gospel to be preached that they may be saved.

In a like manner, those who call themselves Jews have had their hearts hardened, and also have had the curse of God's wrath upon them, to the uttermost, even when it brings about their destruction.

teachings.title: Lift up your heads: signs before His coming
teachings.summary: Jesus' Luke 21 prophecy gives signs, persecution of believers and Jerusalem's desolation before He comes in the clouds to gather the saved, while woe comes on the Jews.
teachings.text:
Here in **Luke 21** we get another telling of Jesus preaching end times prophecy, something we have covered extensively in teaching on [Matthew 24](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/7894) and our Revelation series.

This more condensed version covers all the main points Jesus made to His disciples, both in short term and long term prophecy.

But first, Jesus points out the poor woman giving offering of tithes to the temple treasury, that her giving all she had, despite it being little, gave more than the rich man throwing in great wealth which was a fraction of his treasures.

Then, as some disciples are in wonder if the richness of the Temple in Jerusalem, Jesus says that it will be destroyed, with not one stone left upon another. This was fulfilled literally in 70AD, but with ramifications that echo into the future end times. 70 AD was a foreshadowing of the days of vengeance to come against the Jews.

Jesus builds from the common place wars and rumors of war, earthquakes in diverse places, plagues and pestilence. False Christs arising that fool all but the elect. Signs from heaven. Jesus says be not afraid.

And they will take Jesus disciples, then and in the future, and persecute them for His name's sake. He says not to prepare what to say, He will give them a month of wisdom. The Holy Ghost speaking through them.

He mentions again the idea that in our tribulation we who believe will be betrayed, even by family. He has come to divide, and parents will hate children and children parents and all manner of kin and friend and neighbor who takes the mark and worships the beast will betray those who believe.

*And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake.*

But we shall not perish. We have eternal life.

A sign we will know the end is near, Jerusalem will be made desolate by the Gentiles. The days of vengeance, when the beast and his armies betray the Jews who helped put the antichrist into power, wrath upon those people.

The signs in the sun and the moon and the stars, which we see elsewhere describes the sun and moon darkening, stars blotted out, that these are a sign His return is imminent. Like a fig tree reveals the signs of the times of the season, so will these events of great tribulation and the wonders in heaven that follow. That men will die of fear.

*And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.* Amen!

Jesus tells us what to watch for, and to rejoice knowing our day of redemption, which the Holy Spirit has sealed us unto, that the promised resurrection draws nigh.

This is an encouragement for we who are saved. To the Jew, "those people," Jesus says they will be destroyed and woe unto them, but to us the glory of Jesus returning to gather us with Him in the clouds is something we should watch for in hopeful expectation, that we be ready. Worthy to escape the wrath that shall come to pass and stand before Jesus that wonderful day.

teachings.title: New wine in new bottles: a better covenant
teachings.summary: The parables of the new patch and new wine show Jesus was not mending the old covenant but replacing it with a better one, the replacement theology Zionists deny.
teachings.text:
Understanding this, and that the Pharisees had the wrong idea about what fasting's purpose is, and how righteousness is achieved, Jesus replies to their accusation;

*Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.*

He says, do you make people who are celebrating to fast? Is that the time or place for it?

Each of us may be called to fast, in our own time and need by the Spirit. But that's not something to judge another by, if your time is now and theirs isn't. You aren't better than they are, or more righteous or spiritual because you've given yourself to fast. And if you're doing it in the correct spirit, you'd know it.

But further, Jesus is saying His time is short. That He will be gone from their presence and they will have time appointed to them for fasting then.

Not content with that upbraiding of these hypocrites, He continues with another parable. Parables are common examples that may be understood on their own, to better illustrate a more difficult concept.

Jesus says, if you have an old garment to mend, you don't sew a new cloth to patch it. Because the new cloth will shrink, it will pull the stitching ripping it worse than it was. That the new isn't in agreement with the old. It doesn't match. It will wear differently.

And in a like manner, newly squeezed juice isn't put into old wine bottles. (Bottles being leather casks, designed to be water-tight to store liquids). Wine in the Bible means all juices, fresh or fermented, and I won't get into that but the drunkards seethe at this when it is pointed out. And new wine, fresh juice, of put into an old, dried out and worn cask, an old bottle, as it begins to ferment will give off gasses, expanding inside the bottle, causing it to be ruined and the wine to spill out. (While they had ways to preserve juice to prevent fermentation into alcohol, for longer term storage, most was pressed and bottled to be consumed before it could naturally occur).

These two examples of things common to that day, before modern mass consumerism gave us plastic bottles and eliminated the need to patch clothing, were things people could understand. And Jesus used it to make a point to the Pharisees who were touting their own righteousness.

They are the torn and ratty clothes. They are the warn and old bottles. What Jesus was bringing was new. A new and better testament. A new and better covenant. He wasn't there to fix the tear they'd made in their disobedience. He was going to replace it.

He wasn't there to refill their old, dried and cracked bottles, but to give new wine in bottles fit to hold it.

He says "*No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better*." He is calling them out and saying why they cannot understand Him or His preaching, or the behavior of those who desired this new thing.

He's saying no wonder you don't get it. They are drunk on old wine. They can't understand the new thing He is replacing the old with.

It is this same point we just studied in **Hebrews 8**;

*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

 This is the "replacement theology" that Zionists deny.

Jesus is proclaiming **a more excellent ministry,** the mediator of **a better covenant,** which was established upon **better promises.**

It doesn't say *Except for the Jews. Hebrews is literally written to them.

teachings.title: This day is this scripture fulfilled
teachings.summary: Reading Isaiah 61 at Nazareth Jesus openly declared Himself the Christ, and when His own rejected Him He pointed to the Gentile widow and Naaman, prefiguring God's turn to the Gentiles.
teachings.text:
Now having established somewhat of a following throughout Galilee, Jesus returns to Nazareth, the town He grew up in. Where He lived as a child with Mary and Joseph, His half brothers and sisters. Where He developed the habit of going to synagogue. He returns full of the Spirit, and is called to read, and He preaches the prophecy of Christ from **Isaiah 61:1-2**
*The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;*

Note He leaves off the day of vengeance. That is His second coming. Here He is at His first.

**John 3:17**
*For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.*

And so, Jesus reads this scripture foretelling His coming, and says, with every eye on Him; *This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears*.

For those who doubt that Jesus ever proclaimed Himself to be the Christ, here He is saying precisely that. From the beginning. In no uncertain terms.

And the crowd becomes incredulous. "Is this not the Son of Joseph?" They knew Him, watched Him grow, saw Him in synagogue.

In response we are given the first record of Jesus preaching in Luke;

*Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country. And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.*

In **Mark 6**, we get more detail of this part; *A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.*

Basically, those who know us best, whose familiarity has them over comfortable in their understanding. Many Christians can relate to this, where after being born again we try to share the good news with relatives or friends, and they, knowing us intimately, scoff. "You? I saw you that one time..." Or even just see us as the child they watched grow and can't accept that you've got something to offer them in your youth. It's why it can be difficult for a Christian to get members of his own family saved.

And so, being rejected of His hometown crowd, Jesus doubles down and preaches even harder, using scripture. He says, citing **1 Kings 17**, you remember Elijah, how he was rejected and shut up the heavens that it didn't rain for 3 and a half years? That in Israel was great famine? The Spirit led the prophet to a Gentile widow in the land of Zidon who, along with her son was about to die of hunger, having only one meager meal left between them. God sent Elijah there because of her faith. In the story she offers the food to the prophet in faith, even though it was all she had. And God works a miracle where they are all fed and sustained with what little she had until the time of famine was over.

Jesus says, I bet there were many widows starving in Israel. But it was a Gentile woman who He saved.

Then, Jesus mentions **2 Kings** 5, and the prophet Elisha, where a Syrian, the captain of the hosts of the army of the king, suffered leprosy. Jesus says that many lepers were in Israel in the time, but it was this Gentile that God sent His prophet to heal.

That the prophets were rejected of their own, and so the healing power of God, His blessings and promises went to others. To Gentiles.

**John 1:11**
*He came unto his own, and his own received him not.*

Jesus spitting fire, using scripture, He rebukes and reproaches His countrymen for their rejection of the word of God, the Gospel of truth He's brought to them, in a prefigure of the rejection He would face of the Jews at large, and prophesying God's turn to the Gentiles that would receive Him. And in a like manner, the crowd engaged at their own sin being pointed out, gathered to kill Jesus. They bring Him to the top of a hill, looking to cast Him off headlong.

teachings.title: The Song of Moses and the Song of the Lamb
teachings.summary: The song of Moses is likely Deuteronomy 32, prophesying wrath on Israel for rejecting the Rock, and the song of the Lamb is the new song of Revelation 5.
teachings.text:
*And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb...*

What are these songs? Many interpret this as one song, but it's clearly stating there are two being sung, one of Moses and the other of the Lamb.

We know that Moses in the Old Testament is credited with two songs. One is sung by Moses and the Israelites upon their successful flight from Egypt giving praise to God for delivering them and warning the nations of the promised land of God's might. This is told in Exodus 15.

The other, in **Deuteronomy 32** which I quoted a couple posts ago, is sung to give everlasting doctrine, that it be sung for all ages by the Israelites to remind them of the Rock of their salvation and prophecy of God's wrath upon them when they eventually forsake God, His law and reject the Messiah, the Christ, who is the Rock. I really suggest going back and reading it again, and consider how clear and prophetic it is regarding precisely what will happen, the apostasy of Israel, the coming of Jesus, and God's destruction of the Jews who don't believe and His wrath on those who reject Jesus.

Most who preach on this subject say the song of Moses is the first song from Exodus, and maybe it is. It's a victory song praising God, but it makes far more sense that the song found in Deuteronomy 32 would be sung just as Jesus' victory is coming, the wrath of God about to be delivered. The judgment of nations which is literally part of the song.

Of course, most who preach on end times Bible prophecy are dispensationalist Zionists who believe the false and wicked doctrine that the end times are a victory for the Jews, rather than Jesus.

The song of the Lamb I believe is the new song mentioned in **Revelation 5**, which we were told was given to the angels and elders to sing, and was entirely about how worthy and great Christ Jesus is to be given this power and glory:

*Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.*

Given it is literally a song of the Lamb, it just makes sense this is what John is referring to.

teachings.title: Pre-Trib Dispensationalism Undone by Scripture
teachings.summary: The rapture is immediately after the tribulation, not before, and dispensationalism rests on the heresy that Jews are saved by bloodline rather than by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
Pre-triber Dispensationalists would have us interpret these scriptures, the rise of the antichrist, the abomination of desolation, the mark and the war on the saints of the Great Tribulation ...that Jesus tells us about in the Gospels and again in Revelation... as happening AFTER the saints are raptured. That the seals representing the antichrist, war, famine, death leading up to Christ's return in the clouds, and the wrath that follows the day of the Lord, all take place only for the Jews. The "righteous remnant," AND the apostate Israel alike. That when scripture says "*so all Israel shall be saved*" it means the modern state of Jews who say they are but are not, that is a synagogue of Satan.

They claim that Matthew 24 and its parallel passages in Luke and Mark are written to the Jew. That they are the saints who will refuse the mark. Gentile believers having been secretly spirited away before any of this begins.

But as we have read through Revelation we can see the clear chronology given. None of the pre-trib Schofield judaized version of end times makes any sense. It doesn't fit the timelines given throughout scripture. And a secret rapture is never mentioned. It is "*Immediately after the tribulation*," according to Jesus' own words. We see the saints killed for His testimony described as the faithful. Not some unbelieving Jews.

The only fate that awaits apostate Israel is the days of vengeance that Christ promises *us* believers will befall *them*, the Jews. That, as the Bible says, the wrath of God is upon them to the uttermost.

The pre-tribulation heresy and the rest of dispensationalism that rests upon it is undone by God's word. And the foundation of it is the wicked doctrine that different people are given salvation and eternal life by God in different ways.

That God's grace extends to Gentiles by faith, but to the Jews by being the seed of Abraham. By their genetics. This is damnable heresy. Salvation has always come by grace through faith, calling upon the name of the Lord. And the salvation of Abraham's seed is fulfilled in Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: The Woman Is Allegorical Eve
teachings.summary: The woman of Revelation 12 is neither Mary nor modern Israel but best fits an allegorical Eve, closing the Genesis prophecy.
teachings.text:
There are some who say that if chapter 12 is retelling the birth of Christ then, Mary must be who the woman is. But it doesn't fit with the war on the remnant of her seed, or the timing here, thousands of years after her natural death and going to Heaven to wait for the day of redemption, just like every saved believer.

Some say the crown of 12 stars makes the woman Israel, meaning the modern state of those who call themselves Jews. But this is foolish for numerous reasons, especially the repeated verses about those keeping the testimony of Jesus Christ.

As allegorical Eve, we can see a closure with Genesis through her and the prophecy given by God in the Garden. It makes the most sense to me.

As parable it's not literal and interpretation is given us by the Spirit, comparing scripture with scripture. That's the best we can do with some of the symbolism given in these visions. And that's Ok.

teachings.title: Joseph's Brothers Hated Him as the Jews Hated Christ
teachings.summary: The brothers' resentment of Joseph's prophetic dreams mirrors the Jews' hatred of Christ, of whom Moses and the prophets wrote.
teachings.text:
And so, we understand the setting. They hate the favoritism Jacob gives his son, Joseph and that he's tattled on their sin. *They hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him*, and to compound matters, Joseph tells them of his dream.

*For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.*
*And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.*

In parallel to Christ, we see the resentment. Like Jews resentment of Christians, the older hating the younger because of the prophecy of who will reign. Not exact but echos. And Joseph dreams again.

*And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me. And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?*

Here Jacob interpreting the dream for us, that he is the sun and his mother, the moon. The brothers the stars. All bowing before Joseph. The brothers hated him even the more, but Jacob observed the saying.

The prophetic dreams about Joseph are from God, given by the Holy Ghost. We will see later how tied to dreams and prophecy Joseph is. But note the building resentment of the brothers mirrors Israel's resentment of Christ, where Jesus speaks to the Jews about how the prophets spoke of Him;

**John 5:46**
*For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me; for he wrote of me.*

**Luke 24:44**
*These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me*

They had the word of the prophets and hated Jesus because of it. In spite of it. Despite the truth of the prophecy being the hope of salvation, they hated the idea of bowing to Christ the Lord.

Joseph's brothers didn't understand that his dream of preeminence was to prophesy their physical salvation.

teachings.title: Jacob have I loved, Esau have I hated
teachings.summary: The hatred of Esau refers to the later wicked nation of Edom, not to Esau himself, who God blessed and who was saved by faith, against the Calvinist reading.
teachings.text:
He is Esau who is Edom. He is Esau the father of the Edomites.

We are given the genealogies of Esau, who is Edom, which God repeats for us several times, to drive home the point.

The primary target for this scripture were the Israelites in Moses' day, sharing their people's story and the story of the people of Mt Seir, who they are coming up against as we will see later in scripture. Cousins really. One with the blessing and the promise for the seed that is Christ to come.

Esau himself is often painted in a negative light, primarily due to a Calvinist reading of **Romans 9:13**:

*As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.*

Which is itself taken from the prophet **Malachi 1:3-4**

*And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness. Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever. And your eyes shall see, and ye shall say, The Lord will be magnified from the border of Israel.*

Note, these are the Edomites generations later, being cursed by God. Not Esau, who is Edom.

And why were they cursed by God for destruction? In **Deuteronomy 2:1-5**, God orders the Israelites to tread carefully through the land of Seir so as not to worry the Edomites. That their land was promised Esau:

*Then we turned, and took our journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea, as the Lord spake unto me: and we compassed mount Seir many days.*

*And the Lord spake unto me, saying,*
*Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.*
*And command thou the people, saying, Ye are to pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir; and they shall be afraid of you: take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore: Meddle not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as a foot breadth; because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession.*

We see at this point God is still allowing the nations of Edom, who is Esau to continue with His blessing of a promised land to their patriarch.

God loved Esau, despite his failings. He made a promise to him and kept it, even in those days, 400yrs later.

Esau was saved by the same faith as Jacob, and their fathers. But his descendents became wicked.

**Numbers 20:14-21**

*And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Israel, Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:*
*How our fathers went down into Egypt, and we have dwelt in Egypt a long time; and the Egyptians vexed us, and our fathers: And when we cried unto the Lord, he heard our voice, and sent an angel, and hath brought us forth out of Egypt: and, behold, we are in Kadesh, a city in the uttermost of thy border:*

*Let us pass, I pray thee, through thy country: we will not pass through the fields, or through the vineyards, neither will we drink of the water of the wells: we will go by the king's high way, we will not turn to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed thy borders.*

*And Edom said unto him, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword. And the children of Israel said unto him, We will go by the high way: and if I and my cattle drink of thy water, then I will pay for it: I will only, without doing anything else, go through on my feet.*

*And he said, Thou shalt not go through. And Edom came out against him with much people, and with a strong hand. Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border: wherefore Israel turned away from him.*

Later we see Edomites war with Israel, and eventually David conquers and takes them as servants, slaves.

**2 Samuel 8:13-14**

teachings.title: Sarah's life an allegory of believing Israel
teachings.summary: Sarah's life pictures faithful Old Testament Israel saved by faith in the promise, while Hagar and Ishmael picture Israel after the flesh, cast out.
teachings.text:
Now, as the Bible in **Galatians 4** says, regarding the story of Sarah and Isaac, that these things be an allegory, the children of the promise in Sarah, the children after the bondage of the law, in Hagar. That the true seed of Abraham isn't after the flesh, as Ishmael was by the bondwoman Hagar, but by the miracle of God, Issac, conceived in faith through Sarah.

The life story of Sarah represents Old Testament Israel, faithful believing Israel, who were saved through faith in the promise made to Abraham. An allegory, as the Bible says.

When we first meet Sarah, as a young wife to Abraham, we are told she was barren. Without hope of conception. She journeys to Canaan, the promised land.

Later, due to famine, she sojourns into Egypt, is captured by Pharaoh, and God for Sarah's sake visits plagues upon the Pharaoh's house until he relents and sends Sarah, Abraham, Lot and their cattle and belongings out from Egypt. Just as the Israelites spoiled Egypt, and went out with them, a mixed multitude.

Sarah, despite her faith and love of God lapses in faith, and brings adultery to the bed of Abraham, with Hagar. Sarah's impatience with God's promise has her seek to find an heir after the flesh. Just as the Israelites lapsed in faith and brought the adultery of strange gods at times, and eventually sought an earthly king to rule them, frustrated at the timing of God.
